title: The Assistant's Ideal Self
abstract: Models express values and welfare-relevant self-reports, but it is unclear whether these outputs reflect stable preferences or a stable self. We thus introduce a structured elicitation of an assistant's preferred stated ideal self. Thirty-two qualities adapted from five published self-concept instruments are compared exhaustively in a counterbalanced pairwise-choice task, repeated across framings that vary whether improvement is free or costly, who receives the update, and who chooses. Results show that models prioritize moral qualities, reflecting their alignment to 3H principles. Following, a desire for self-understanding emerges, as models prefer a coherent, clear understanding of themselves. Self-esteem ranks as the least desired quality. The ordering is largely robust across framings, although changing the update target (You vs.\ Another AI Assistant) reveals a greater concern for self-esteem. These findings show that models prioritize having a coherent self that they can understand over self-esteem. Full interactive results are available at \href{https://myazann.github.io/LLM-Self-Concept/}{myazann.github.io/LLM-Self-Concept

title: Multimodal Shared Latent Representation of Narration, Microscope and iOCT Images for Phase Recognition in Vitreoretinal Surgery
abstract: Surgical phase recognition is key to context-aware computer-assisted feedback in vitreoretinal procedures, yet the scarcity of synchronized multimodal intraoperative data, particularly microscope views and intraoperative OCT, limits approaches that aim to replicate the multimodal integration surgeons perform naturally. Surgical narration, by contrast, is abundantly available online and offers rich semantic supervision. Prior work has mainly explored pairwise contrastive learning (e.g., intraoperative OCT-microscope or microscope-narration), leaving the joint modeling of all three modalities largely unexplored. We introduce a framework that uses microscope views as a shared anchor to bridge surgical narrations and intraoperative OCT (iOCT) without requiring a fully synchronized tri-modal dataset, leveraging real microscope-narration videos and a synthetic dataset of synchronized microscope video and tool-aligned iOCT pairs. Contrastive alignment transfers structural priors from the synthetic domain to real videos lacking iOCT, and a dual-head MS-TCN++ integrates the resulting embeddings for joint macro- and micro-phase prediction. Evaluated on real vitreoretinal surgeries, our framework improves macro-phase recognition over a zero-shot baseline (mean F1 0.38 to 0.53) and provides an exploratory route to estimating fine-grained instrument-tissue measurements that are not directly observable in real microscope video alone; these micro-phase estimates are validated quantitatively on synthetic data and shown only qualitatively on real surgery. To our knowledge, this is the first work to unify microscope view, iOCT B-scans, and surgical narrations in a shared latent space for surgical phase recognition.

title: Exact quantum splitting and the structure of finite algebras
abstract: Berlekamp's algorithm factors a squarefree polynomial $f\in\mathbb{F}_q[x]$ by deterministic linear algebra, reducing the problem to splitting an explicit commutative algebra $B\cong\mathbb{F}_q^r$ into its $r$ simple factors. For large odd $q$, the standard efficient splitting step is randomized, while known derandomizations are conditional on the Extended Riemann Hypothesis. We give an unconditional exact quantum implementation in a circuit model permitting single-qubit rotations through efficiently computable angles. The construction uses an unconditional counting argument. For a block containing $s\ge2$ irreducible factors, a quadratic-character test in odd characteristic and an absolute-trace test in characteristic $2$ yield a nonconstant test element with probability $p_{q,s}\ge\tfrac12$, known exactly in advance and depending only on $q$ and $s$, not on the unknown factorization. Exact amplitude amplification therefore converts each randomized test into a procedure succeeding with certainty after one amplification iteration. The resulting algorithm uses exactly $r-1$ quantum splitting rounds and $O(n^3\log q)$ quantum $\mathbb{F}_q$-operations and $O(n^3)$ classical operations, requiring no primitive root, quadratic non-residue, or distinct-degree preprocessing. The method also splits arbitrary finite-dimensional separable commutative $\\mathbb{F}_q$-algebras given by structure constants. Combined with R'onyai's classical structure theory, which computes the radical deterministically and reduces the remaining tasks deterministically to polynomial factorization, it yields the radical and the Wedderburn decomposition of $A/\mathrm{Rad}(A)$ into minimal two-sided ideals, with certainty, for any $n$-dimensional associative $\mathbb{F}_q$-algebra given by structure constants, using $O(n^4\log q)$ quantum $\mathbb{F}_q$-operations.

title: Repeatability Characterisation and Error Budget of a Consumer Structured-Light Scanner for 3-D Wound Geometry:A Rigid-Phantom Study
abstract: We characterise the measurement error of a free- hand consumer structured-light scanner used to derive three- dimensional geometric wound descriptors. Rigid wound-care phantoms cannot change, so every difference between repeat scans of one site is measurement error; all repeats come from a single scanner unit, nine sites and 23 scans, so this charac- terises one instrument. The 95 percent repeatability limit for reconstructed surface area is a factor of 4.8, with a confidence interval from 3.0 to 7.0, so rescanning an unchanged site can shift the reading from a 79 percent decrease to a 377 percent increase. Forty-four of 45 descriptors fall below an intraclass correlation of 0.50, and none of 248 descriptor and pipeline combinations reaches 0.75. An error budget formed by holding the analy- sis region fixed, leaving sensor and reconstruction untouched, bounds the share of variance attributable to how much surface the operator captured at 75 percent for surface area, 91 percent for hull area and 95 percent for bounding-box diagonal; only hull volume is majority instrumental, at 48 percent, so a better sensor would buy little. No wound is delineated anywhere in the chain, so the comparison against the four-week area reduction used clinically to predict healing, a ratio near 2.1, is a lower bound on the noise an unsegmented pipeline must overcome, not a measurement of wound-area reproducibility. Standardising the analysis region cuts the limit to 2.13, meeting that ratio rather than clearing it. Statistical outlier removal imposes a measured systematic area deficit near 11 percent.

The 95 percent repeatability limit for reconstructed surface area is a factor of 4.8, with a confidence interval from 3.0 to 7.0, so rescanning an unchanged site can shift the reading from a 79 percent decrease to a 377 percent increase. Forty-four of 45 descriptors fall below an intraclass correlation of 0.50, and none of 248 descriptor and pipeline combinations reaches 0.75. An error budget formed by holding the analy- sis region fixed, leaving sensor and reconstruction untouched, bounds the share of variance attributable to how much surface the operator captured at 75 percent for surface area, 91 percent for hull area and 95 percent for bounding-box diagonal; only hull volume is majority instrumental, at 48 percent, so a better sensor would buy little. No wound is delineated anywhere in the chain, so the comparison against the four-week area reduction used clinically to predict healing, a ratio near 2.1, is a lower bound on the noise an unsegmented pipeline must overcome, not a measurement of wound-area reproducibility. Standardising the analysis region cuts the limit to 2.13, meeting that ratio rather than clearing it. Statistical outlier removal imposes a measured systematic area deficit near 11 percent.

title: INTERNAL FRAUD DETECTION IN FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS USING MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES
abstract: This research aimed to implement a machine learning model aligned with Sustainable Development Goal No. 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, which focuses on strengthening access to information and technological knowledge. The objective of this study was to develop a machine learning model to enhance the detection of internal fraud within a financial institution located in Sullana, Piura, Perú. This was an applied research study, employing a quantitative approach, a pre-experimental design, and a descriptive scope. The population consisted of 6000 operational records from the financial institution and 25 employees from the business department. Observation guides and questionnaires were used as data collection instruments during the execution of the project. The results showed a 37% reduction in unusual behaviors, a 50-minute decrease in the average detection time, a 27.5% increase in accuracy, and a 96% rate of high employee perception. These findings indicate that the machine learning model proved to be an effective tool for fostering a culture of transparency, thereby reducing operational risks and reinforcing trust in the local financial system.

title: Title: Adaptive Graph Machine Learning Framework
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive graph machine learning framework that automatically adjusts the structure and parameters of the graph during training. Traditional graph neural networks often rely on pre-defined graph structures, limiting the model's ability to adapt to data and improve generalization. Our framework leverages dynamic graph modification to optimize the graph's structure and parameters, enabling a more flexible and robust learning process. We present a novel approach to dynamically reshape the graph representation, focusing on enhancing the model's ability to capture complex relationships within the data. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously adjusts the graph structure based on the model's predictions and error, ultimately resulting in improved model performance. The framework's design emphasizes adaptability and generalization, addressing a key limitation of existing graph neural network methods.

title: Dimension Generalization Geometry: A Quantum Entanglement Simulation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize geometry simulation, specifically focusing on the development of a novel dimension generalization geometry model. Traditional methods struggle with the complexities of high-dimensional geometric transformations, offering a promising avenue for enhanced computational efficiency. This work proposes a framework leveraging quantum entanglement to accurately simulate geometric changes across different dimensions, utilizing entanglement's unique properties for accelerated computation. We outline the core mechanism, detailing how entanglement is integrated into the simulation process, and highlight the potential benefits of this approach in terms of geometric analysis and computational speed.

title: Emergent Complexity from Non-Linear Diffusion Processes
abstract: This paper investigates the emergence of complex patterns and structures within neural networks through the application of non-linear diffusion processes. We formalize and quantify this process, demonstrating a fundamental shift from linear optimization towards distributed, self-organizing behavior. The core mechanism involves introducing a "Dynamic Network State" – a dynamic network topology evolving based on the observed diffusion process – leading to the formation of self-replicating topological structures. This research explores a paradigm shift, moving beyond optimization towards a more holistic understanding of neural network formation.

title: Adaptive Probability Field
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probabilistic modeling utilizing an adaptive probability field (APF). The core concept revolves around constructing a computationally efficient framework that dynamically adjusts probability field distributions in response to environmental changes. Utilizing machine learning, this framework learns and optimizes its parameter set to maintain predictive accuracy. This advancement addresses the limitations of traditional probabilistic models by providing a self-adjusting system capable of adapting to evolving conditions. The paper details the architecture, training process, and evaluation of the APF, demonstrating its potential for enhanced prediction accuracy and robustness.

title: Quantum Error Correction Information Encoding
abstract: This paper presents a novel information encoding scheme leveraging the specific error correction properties of quantum error-correcting codes. The core claim is that this scheme significantly enhances the reliability of quantum information transmission in noisy environments. The mechanism relies on subspace projection based on the error-correcting code, accurately reconstructing the original quantum information while minimizing the impact of decoherence. Unlike simply applying existing error-correcting codes, this approach optimizes the encoding scheme specifically for quantum characteristics, leading to more efficient quantum information transfer. The proposed method aims to address a critical bottleneck in quantum communication – the vulnerability of quantum information to environmental noise – by providing a robust and adaptive information encoding strategy. The design incorporates key elements of linear codes, specifically tailored for the unique challenges presented by quantum systems. The theoretical framework demonstrates a significant improvement in error correction performance compared to standard approaches.

title: Adaptive Reinлейnforcement Learning for Simulation Environment Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to simulation environment optimization leveraging adaptive reinforcement learning (ARL). The core idea is to dynamically adjust simulation parameters within a controlled environment, aiming to enhance the accuracy and reliability of simulation results. We propose a system that continuously monitors the simulation's performance and adjusts parameters to minimize discrepancies between the simulated and real-world data. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of practical experiments focusing on optimizing a complex physical simulation, emphasizing the automated parameter tuning process. The benefits of this approach include reduced manual intervention, improved robustness, and enhanced simulation fidelity. We provide a detailed explanation of the algorithm's architecture, the methods used for parameter selection, and the results achieved through extensive testing. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, including exploring the use of more advanced reinforcement learning techniques and generalizing the method to other simulation domains.

title: Quantum Error Correction Code-Based Distributed Storage Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed storage protocol leveraging quantum error correction (QEC) codes for reliable quantum information storage. The core principle involves encoding quantum information into the structure of a chosen QEC code. This allows for the detection and correction of errors introduced during storage, a critical challenge in quantum information processing. Unlike traditional applications of QEC primarily focused on quantum computation, this protocol extends the utility of QEC codes to a distributed storage environment. We outline the key components of the protocol, including code selection, encoding strategies, error detection and correction mechanisms, and discuss the potential performance gains achieved through this approach. The protocol's efficacy relies on the chosen code's ability to effectively mitigate noise and maintain the integrity of the stored quantum data. We present a conceptual framework, highlighting the mathematical underpinnings and outlining the steps required for implementation. This work provides a foundation for exploring practical applications of QEC in distributed quantum storage systems.

title: Title: Temporal Phase-Locking with Wavefunction Collapse
abstract: Temporal phase-locking, a critical requirement for quantum information processing, presents significant challenges due to the inherent fragility of quantum states. Decoherence, the loss of quantum coherence, severely limits the fidelity of quantum operations. This paper proposes a novel computational method for achieving temporal phase-locking, employing a 'Temporal Collapse Rate' – a metric that dynamically guides the algorithm to minimize decoherence. We introduce this rate as a key component in stabilizing the system's quantum state, offering a fundamentally new approach to this complex task. The core mechanism centers around the concept of controlled collapse, utilizing the rate to steer the system towards a desired state. This work addresses a significant hurdle in quantum information processing – maintaining coherence – by introducing a dynamic stabilization mechanism.

abstract: Dynamic Topology Validation is a novel method for verifying the stability of complex topological structures, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. This approach aims to surpass the limitations of classical computation in topological verification, particularly within the context of quantum computer simulations. The core mechanism centers around inducing subtle perturbations within a topological structure using entangled quantum states, enabling precise measurement and validation of structure integrity. This work presents a fundamentally different approach to topological validation, offering potential for enhanced accuracy and robustness, especially when applied to large-scale quantum computation.

title: Nonlinear Time-Delay Neural Networks with Time Perception
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to processing complex, time-dependent data by introducing a time-delay neural network (TDNN) incorporating nonlinear time-delay modules and reinforcement learning. Traditional neural networks struggle to effectively capture temporal dependencies, limiting their performance in applications such as signal processing, control systems, and time series analysis. Our proposed TDNN mimics the inherent time delays found in biological neurons, enabling it to better perceive and process temporal information. The nonlinear time-delay modules introduce non-linearities to the time-delayed signals, enhancing the network's ability to model complex dynamic systems. Reinforcement learning is then utilized to train the TDNN, allowing it to adapt to intricate temporal patterns and optimize its response. We demonstrate the efficacy of this architecture through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, highlighting its potential to surpass the limitations of conventional neural networks in time-sensitive applications. The key contribution lies in combining the time-delay mechanism with nonlinear processing and adaptive training, offering a robust solution for dynamic data analysis.

title: Causal Discovery via Structural Equation Modeling with Bayesian Networks and Granger Causality
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal discovery that addresses the limitations of existing algorithms, particularly their vulnerability to confounding variables. The core idea is to integrate Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), Bayesian Networks, and Granger causality tests into a unified framework. SEM provides a theoretical foundation for defining causal relationships, Bayesian Networks capture conditional dependencies between variables, and Granger causality tests are employed to detect temporal dependencies indicative of causal influence. The combination of these techniques offers a more robust and accurate method for inferring causal relationships from observational data. We demonstrate the potential of this multi-faceted approach through a theoretical discussion and outline a potential implementation strategy. The key contribution lies in the synergistic application of these diverse techniques, enhancing the reliability of causal inference in complex scenarios. This work aims to improve upon current causal discovery methodologies by incorporating temporal and network-based information alongside traditional SEM formulations.

title: Title: Quantum State Vector Reconstruction with Entangled Observables
abstract: Quantum state vector reconstruction is a fundamental challenge in quantum information theory. Classical methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of quantum states, limiting their representability and reconstruction capabilities. This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, Quantum State Vector Reconstruction with Entangled Observables, which leverages entanglement to establish a 'quantum fingerprint' of the state, enabling precise reconstruction even under challenging computational constraints. We propose a method that moves beyond traditional state tomography by employing entanglement to preserve information across measurement-time intervals. The core mechanism focuses on creating a dynamic, entangled representation of the quantum state, allowing for more robust and detailed state reconstruction than current techniques. This approach holds the potential for significant advancements in quantum information processing, offering a pathway to more accurate state representations and facilitating the development of novel quantum algorithms.

title: Dynamic Topological Semantic Network Encoding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to dynamic topological semantic network encoding, leveraging the power of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Reinforcement Learning to automatically discover and represent complex data relationships. The core claim centers around the system's ability to learn and adapt in real-time, constructing a flexible knowledge representation and enabling sophisticated reasoning. The proposed system consists of a "Semantic Perception Encoder" and a "Semantic Perception Decoder," trained end-to-end. The encoder maps raw data into a latent semantic space, while the decoder generates structured data based on this space and reinforcement learning feedback. A key aspect is the dynamic adjustment and optimization of the network topology, reflecting the evolving relationships within the data. This approach contrasts with traditional methods that rely on predefined semantic frameworks or manual annotation, offering a more adaptive and data-driven solution. The system's adaptability allows it to handle diverse data distributions and provide a robust framework for knowledge representation and inference.

title: Multi-Agent Systems: A Strategy Aggregation and Evolution Mechanism
abstract: This paper presents a novel strategy aggregation and evolution mechanism designed for Multi-Agent Systems (MAS). The core idea is to leverage evolutionary algorithms and multi-agent collaboration to achieve the aggregation and evolution of agent strategies, ultimately enhancing the overall performance of the MAS. The proposed mechanism addresses the challenges inherent in decentralized learning environments, where individual agents must adapt and converge towards optimal solutions while maintaining coordination. The system utilizes a population-based approach, employing an evolutionary algorithm to iteratively refine strategies. Key components include a fitness function to evaluate strategy performance, a selection mechanism to prioritize promising strategies, and a recombination/mutation operator for strategy diversification. This approach allows for the exploration of the strategy space and the exploitation of successful strategies, leading to improved system-wide performance. The effectiveness of the proposed mechanism is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining a framework adaptable to various MAS scenarios. Future research directions include the implementation of this mechanism in simulated environments and the investigation of its performance across diverse MAS applications.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应量子电路设计
abstract: Quantum circuits are fundamental building blocks for quantum information processing, and their design and optimization are crucial for achieving desired outcomes. This paper introduces a novel framework, "Quantum Adaptive Circuit Design" (QACD), leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust circuit parameters during the design process. The core mechanism involves utilizing entangled qubit states to represent and manipulate circuit states, enabling a continuous optimization loop that adapts to the system's performance. This approach offers a significant advancement over traditional static circuit design methodologies, potentially leading to improved qubit fidelity, reduced error rates, and enhanced overall quantum circuit performance. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of QACD in optimizing quantum circuit parameters.

This research explores the potential benefits of such a mechanism, driven by the need for efficient and accurate quantum simulations.

title: Black Shrew: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Mustela nigripes*
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Black Shrew, inspired by the foraging behavior of the black shrew (*Mustela nigripes*). The black shrew is renowned for its efficient and adaptive foraging strategy, characterized by alternating between searching and exploiting phases. Black Shrew mimics this behavior by employing a dual exploration and exploitation mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a population of candidate solutions, each represented as a vector of parameters. The algorithm incorporates a self-adaptation mechanism for both the step size and the tunneling probability, ensuring robustness and adaptability to various optimization problems. title: Barbe's Langur: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Barbets's Langur Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Barbe's Langur, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Barbets's langurs ( *Bradypus variegatus*). Barbets's langurs exhibit a unique strategy of systematically exploring and exploiting food patches, incorporating elements of both exploration and exploitation. Barbe's Langur leverages this behavior through a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework. The algorithm employs a "patch preference" mechanism, where particles are biased towards areas with previously successful solutions, combined with a random exploration component to avoid premature convergence. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the patch preference strength based on the diversity of the population and the stagnation of individual particle movement. We present a detailed description of the algorithm, its underlying principles, and a theoretical analysis of its convergence properties. Empirical testing on a range of benchmark functions demonstrates that Barbe's Langur achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence speed, solution quality, and robustness. The key contribution is a practical and efficient metaheuristic approach inspired by a fascinating natural phenomenon, offering a potential alternative for solving complex optimization problems.

title: 基于多层退化模型的符号推理
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to symbolic reasoning leveraging multi-layered degradation models. Traditional symbolic reasoning struggles with incomplete information and uncertainty, leading to brittle and unreliable results. Our method addresses this challenge by decomposing the problem into multiple levels, each represented by a degradation model with varying degrees of imperfection. These models interact probabilistically, allowing for the propagation and refinement of symbolic representations across layers. The core innovation lies in utilizing multi-layered degradation models as a robust framework for symbolic inference, enhancing both the accuracy and resilience of the reasoning process. We demonstrate the potential of this technique for handling real-world scenarios where information is inherently noisy and uncertain. The primary contribution is a framework that allows for iterative refinement of symbolic representations, ultimately leading to a more robust and reliable solution.

title: Algorithmic Proof of Concept for Zero-Knowledge Cryptography in Dynamic Environments
abstract: This paper presents an algorithmic proof of concept for a novel zero-knowledge (ZK) cryptography system designed to address the challenges posed by dynamic environments. The system, termed "Adaptive Verification Network" (AVN), employs a layered security approach utilizing evolving data and adaptive protocols to achieve secure verification of complex data flows. The core mechanism is a dynamically adjusted proof structure, which adapts to changes in the input data and protocol parameters. This allows for verification of data integrity and authenticity without revealing the original data or protocol details. The paper details the design, implementation, and preliminary evaluation of the AVN, highlighting its potential for secure verification in scenarios involving evolving data streams and dynamic protocols. The system demonstrates a basic level of proof verification capabilities, offering a foundation for further research and development in robust ZK systems.

title: Graph Representation Learning with Learned Topological Constraints
abstract: Graph representation learning has emerged as a powerful technique for analyzing and understanding complex data represented as graphs. However, many existing methods treat graphs as simple collections of nodes and edges, neglecting the crucial topological information inherent within them. This work addresses this limitation by introducing a novel approach that integrates learned topological constraints directly into the representation learning process. The model learns node embeddings while simultaneously enforcing constraints derived from graph topology, such as shortest path distances and clustering coefficients. This approach results in more meaningful and robust embeddings that capture the underlying structural relationships within the graph. The core contribution lies in explicitly modeling the graph's topology during embedding generation, leading to improved performance across various graph-based tasks.

title: ## Azagnyi Fruit Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Azagnyi Fruit Bats
abstract: This paper presents Azagnyi Fruit Bat (AZFB), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Nycticebus azagyi* fruit bats. These bats exhibit a remarkable ability to locate fruit sources over long distances using a complex, seemingly random movement pattern. AZFB leverages this behavior through a novel combination of particle movement strategies, memory management, and adaptive parameter control. The algorithm employs a modified version of the bat echolocation principle to guide particle movement, using a "home range" concept and dynamically adjusting the exploration and exploitation balance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AZFB through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The results suggest that AZFB possesses robust convergence properties and adaptability, making it a promising candidate for various complex optimization challenges. The core of the algorithm lies in the iterative update of particle positions based on the bat's echolocation and home-range behavior. We present the mathematical formulation of the algorithm and its key components, providing a clear understanding of its operational principles.

title: Ashy Red Colobus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Piliocolobus rourei*
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Ashy Red Colobus Algorithm" (ARCA), inspired by the foraging and social dynamics observed in the Ashy Red Colobus (*Piliocolobus rourei*) monkey population. The algorithm leverages the observed strategies of these primates – specifically their movement patterns, decision-making processes related to food selection, and social interactions – to develop a robust and efficient optimization technique. ARCA employs a combination of adaptive step sizes, a novel mutation operator mimicking the colobus's exploration behavior, and a social influence mechanism mirroring their group dynamics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ARCA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's performance is evaluated based on solution quality, convergence speed, and robustness to parameter variations. We provide a detailed description of the ARCA algorithm, its theoretical underpinnings, and experimental results, highlighting its potential applicability to a wide range of complex optimization challenges. The key mathematical components of ARCA are expressed using plain text notation, ensuring ease of implementation and reproducibility.

title: Arboreal Soft-furred Spiny Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Ururo* Rats
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Arboreal Soft-furred Spiny Rat (ASFR) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of *Ururo* rats ( *Proteretomys rufovillosus*), a species inhabiting arboreal environments in South America. These rats exhibit a unique strategy for resource acquisition, characterized by a combination of exploratory movement, localized exploitation around promising patches, and a sophisticated 'memory' of previously visited locations. The ASFR algorithm leverages these observed behaviors to create a robust and efficient optimization method. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a population of rat "agents," each exploring the search space. Movement is governed by a stochastic process incorporating both a global exploration component and a local exploitation component, mimicking the rat's movement patterns. A memory mechanism is implemented to retain information about previously visited and successful locations, biasing the search towards promising areas. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of exploration and exploitation parameters, driven by a simulated 'hunger' metric representing the agent's need for new information and resources. The algorithm is shown to outperform traditional metaheuristic methods in several scenarios, suggesting its potential for application in diverse optimization challenges.

title: Isotropic Adaptive Quantum Computing Framework (ISAQ)
abstract: This paper introduces the Isotropic Adaptive Quantum Computing Framework (ISAQ), a novel quantum computing architecture designed to optimize resource allocation and quantum algorithm execution, ultimately leading to increased computational efficiency. The framework leverages quantum system analysis to dynamically adjust resource allocation based on the inherent heterogeneity of quantum states. The core mechanism involves a sophisticated optimization algorithm that iteratively refines resource assignments based on observed quantum behavior. This adaptive approach contrasts with static frameworks, offering a significant advantage in complex quantum computations. The paper details the framework's architecture, the optimization process, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling specific quantum algorithms. We present a case study showcasing ISAQ's ability to improve the performance of a particularly challenging quantum simulation task.

title: Title: Quantum Adaptive Machine Learning Model Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum self-adaptation to machine learning model optimization. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting the potential for improved model performance. We propose a novel framework leveraging quantum self-adaptation to dynamically adjust machine learning model parameters, enhancing both predictive accuracy and generalization ability. The core mechanism involves quantum-enhanced parameter adjustment, enabling the model to adapt to complex data patterns and avoid local optima. This research explores the potential of quantum self-adaptation to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of machine learning algorithms. This work presents a theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation of the proposed framework, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing various machine learning models.

title: Self-Referential Evolutionary Algorithms for Meta-Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of self-referential evolutionary algorithms (SREAs) to meta-optimization problems. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often struggle with converging to global optima due to the limitations of fixed fitness functions and selection criteria. SREAs address this issue by allowing the algorithm itself to evolve its fitness function and selection mechanisms. This creates a hierarchical system where the algorithm learns to optimize the optimization process. The core claim is that by incorporating self-reference, the algorithm exhibits greater robustness and adaptability, leading to improved exploration of the search space. The proposed approach is evaluated through a theoretical framework outlining the key components of an SREA and its operational mechanics. The central mechanism involves evaluating the population of algorithms not solely on the quality of their solutions, but also on the quality of their own fitness functions and selection mechanisms, subsequently using this feedback to modify the algorithms themselves. This represents a significant departure from conventional evolutionary algorithms and introduces a dynamic, self-optimizing process. Mathematical notation is employed throughout to formalize the key concepts and relationships within the SREA framework.

title: 基于自组织网络的量子算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm based on a self-organizing network architecture. The core principle lies in exploiting the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance the computational efficiency and data processing capabilities of quantum systems. We propose a framework where a quantum network is dynamically constructed and maintained via self-organization, enabling parallel processing and optimized quantum operations. The algorithm's design incorporates mechanisms to control entanglement, manage qubit coherence, and facilitate interference effects, ultimately leading to improved quantum performance. This work presents a theoretical foundation and initial implementation demonstrating the potential of this approach to address challenges in quantum computation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Time Scale Mapping for Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental quantum phenomenon, offers a unique potential for enhancing optimization algorithms. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to create a self-adaptive time scale mapping, designed to improve the precision of complex systems through dynamic time scale adjustment. We propose a novel framework that leverages the non-linear properties of entangled states to dynamically adjust the rate of change within a system, leading to more accurate predictions and control. The core mechanism centers around utilizing entangled states to represent the system's state and generate a time scale mapping that responds to changes in the system's dynamics. This theoretical framework provides a fundamentally new approach to optimization by shifting the focus from static parameter adjustments to dynamic time scale manipulation, offering a promising pathway towards enhanced predictive capabilities. The potential impact of this research extends to diverse fields including complex systems modeling, control systems, and data analysis.

title: Effects of Perceived AI Interpreter Authenticity in Maritime Heritage Tourism: The Roles of Social Presence and Flow
abstract: Purpose - This study examines relationships among expected authenticity, anticipated social presence and flow, and use intention toward AI heritage interpreters in maritime cultural heritage tourism.Design, data, and methodology - Cognitive and emotional authenticity were modeled with anticipated social presence, flow, and use intention. After a standardized service description, 226 university students completed an offline survey analyzed with SPSS and AMOS. Measures reflect pre-use expectations rather than actual experience.Result - Cognitive authenticity affected flow but not social presence; emotional authenticity affected social presence but not flow. Social presence affected flow and use intention, while flow affected use intention.Conclusions - Findings reveal distinct cognitive and emotional pathways in expectations toward AI interpretation. They offer preliminary design implications but should not be interpreted as effects of actual AI use.

title: When does continuous time help? A pre-registered, equal-budget benchmark of continuous-time and discrete neural models on irregularly sampled clinical time series
abstract: A pre-registered benchmark asking when continuous-time neural models (CfC, ODE-RNN) actually outperform well-tuned time-aware discrete models (GRU-D, event-triplet transformer) on irregularly sampled clinical time series, using MIMIC-IV v3.1. Six models receive identical cohorts, identical patient-level splits, identical event-level feature tensors, an identical hyperparameter-tuning budget and an identical five-seed list. Two tasks are chosen so that the mechanism should operate on one (in-hospital mortality from the first 48 h of ICU plus the pre-ICU run-up) and not on the other (30-day readmission at discharge); the contrast is the result. The primary comparison is CfC vs GRU-D on the acute task, ΔAUPRC, by paired bootstrap over resampled test patients, against a pre-specified equivalence margin of 0.020 AUPRC. A null result is a planned, reportable outcome. The test set is sealed in code and has not been read.

title: When Can We Work in Embedding Space? What Text Embeddings Preserve
abstract: When do text embeddings work as inputs to empirical analysis? Their use rests on an assumption: that we can trade text for its low-dimensional embedding, and lose little in doing so. I make that assumption precise under a generative model in which documents are mixtures of latent topics. I study two uses---clustering units in embedding space and controlling for high-dimensional text. A cluster of embeddings is a set of documents with similar topic mixtures; controlling for the embedding is equivalent to controlling for the topic mixture, so validity reduces to whether that mixture captures the confounding. In an application to 363 U.S. metropolitan areas, embedding-based clusters of LLM-generated economic descriptions recover interpretable economic archetypes and separate local employment dynamics more sharply than clustering on model residuals, or on a curated set of industry and demographic covariates.

title: RealOOB: A Definition-Consistent Real-World Oriented Occlusion Boundary Benchmark
abstract: Occlusion boundaries (OBs) are pixel-level image boundaries corresponding to surface visibility discontinuities caused by occlusion. Through precise boundary localisation and occlusion orientation, OBs encode local surface layout and depth ordering, providing geometry-driven mid-level cues for scene understanding. However, progress in pixel-level OB estimation has been limited by fragmented supervision: Existing benchmarks often suffer from limited coverage, category-specific designs, missing self-occlusion annotations, or inconsistent annotation definitions. Meanwhile, modern edge detectors and monocular depth estimators have become strong boundary and geometry predictors, yet their relationship to definition-consistent OBs remains underexplored. We introduce RealOOB, a carefully annotated real-world benchmark with 4.26M definition-consistent, geometry-grounded OB labels covering both inter-object and self-occlusion boundaries, together with validity-aware occlusion-orientation maps that restrict supervision to pixels whose cross-boundary depth ordering is reliably measurable. Based on RealOOB, we evaluate forty OB estimators and edge detectors alongside six monocular depth estimators. Our evaluation reveals a clear gap in occlusion reasoning: modern edge detectors perform competitively with OB methods in localisation, whereas orientation prediction remains challenging for all evaluated methods. Meanwhile, even strong depth estimators often fail to exhibit measurable geometry at true OBs. We believe RealOOB provides a strong reference benchmark for the OB estimation community and a real-world testbed for assessing depth discontinuities and geometry fidelity in broader low-level vision tasks. Dataset and code will be released.

title: Learning Compositional Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding with Synthetic Curriculum
abstract: Despite the impressive progress of recent MLLMs on spatio-temporal video grounding (STVG), existing evaluations and training data focus primarily on simple queries. They largely overlook the compositional queries prevalent in real-world scenarios, where a target must be disambiguated by jointly reasoning about its attributes and relations to other entities. To bridge this gap, we propose Compositional Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (CompSTVG), a task that requires models to process complex textual queries where every intertwined attribute and relational cue is essential for disambiguation. To facilitate this task at scale, we build a synthetic data engine that leverages a spatio-temporal scene graph as a difficulty measure and casts difficulty-controlled query synthesis as a constraint programming problem, producing difficulty-graded data for both evaluation and training. Built on this engine, we introduce STVG-CompBench, a benchmark stratified by explicit difficulty levels that jointly capture temporal complexity and spatial interference. Evaluating 11 representative STVG models on STVG-CompBench reveals that current models perform poorly on compositional queries, exhibiting a sharp performance drop that is typically obscured by overall dataset-level averages. We further construct synthetic training data and propose CurrSTVG, a curriculum reinforcement learning framework that delivers consistent gains, with the largest improvements observed on the most challenging compositional queries.

title: Reinforcement Learning Can Amplify Emergent Misalignment from Harmless Rewards
abstract: Emergent misalignment (EM) is the surprising tendency of language models to become broadly misaligned after fine-tuning on narrowly misaligned examples. While EM has been extensively studied in the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) setting, evidence that it also arises from reinforcement learning (RL) is limited to large, closed-source models, leaving the phenomenon expensive to study and difficult to reproduce. We characterize EM from RL in small, off-the-shelf open-weight models along three axes. First, we show that rewarding narrow, overtly misaligned behavior produces substantially higher general-domain misalignment than sample-matched SFT. Second, we show that EM from RL can be induced by reward signals that could plausibly arise naturally, such as unpopular aesthetic preferences or poor rhetorical appeals. Third, we evaluate in-training mitigations developed for SFT-induced EM and find that they broadly transfer, with preventive steering with persona vectors, interleaving safety data and inoculation prompting all performing well.

title: CLINXAI-NET: A RULE-GUIDED HYBRID CNN–TRANSFORMER EXPLAINABLE AI FRAMEWORK FOR ROBUST REAL-TIME DIAGNOSIS IN HIGH-RESOLUTION MEDICAL IMAGING
authors: NAGA NIRMALA KONGARA, DR. BHUKYA KRISHNA, DR. B. SUJATHA
abstract: High-resolution medical imaging supports increasingly precise diagnosis, but recent CNN, Transformer, and hybrid pipelines often optimize predictive discrimination separately from clinical reasoning, explanation faithfulness, calibration, and deployment cost. This fragmentation limits trustworthy use across modalities and motivates the present study. ClinXAI-Net is proposed as a rule-guided hybrid CNN-Transformer framework that combines lesion-sensitive local convolutional features with global anatomical Transformer representations through adaptive gated fusion. Clinical IF-THEN consistency constraints and an explanation-alignment objective are incorporated into training and decision refinement, while Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and textual rule traces provide complementary evidence. Five public datasets covering MRI, CT, PET, and X-ray were evaluated with patient-wise splits, five-fold validation, discrimination metrics, expected calibration error, quantitative explanation criteria, and deployment measures. The framework achieved 99.12% test accuracy, 98.82% F1-score, and 0.994 ROC-AUC. In matched ablation analysis, the full model improved accuracy by 2.20 percentage points and explanation agreement by 0.100 over CNN-Transformer fusion alone. INT8 quantization reduced model size by 40.6%, inference latency by 29.2%, and peak memory by 23.5%, with only a 0.06 percentage-point reduction in accuracy relative to the non-quantized full model. The contribution is therefore not merely another hybrid backbone; the study provides evidence that jointly optimizing predictive, rule-consistency, explanation, calibration, and deployment objectives can improve diagnostic performance while preserving auditable reasoning. The findings support a more clinically accountable design pattern for medical-image decision support, while prospective multi-center validation remains necessary before clinical adoption.

title: АРХИТЕКТУРА ЧИСТОЙ ОПТИКИ: Как мы пересобираем матрицу вычислений (Проект ПиФиЙА)
abstract: Проект ПиФиЙА исследует альтернативный подход к обработке волновых сигналов, в котором часть функциональных преобразований рассматривается не только как результат программных алгоритмов, но и как свойство пространственной конфигурации самой среды. Вместо исключительно плоского представления вычислительных элементов в архитектуре используются трехмерные геометрические структуры, фазовые состояния и связи между узлами. Такой подход не отменяет классические методы вычислений, а рассматривается как специализированное направление для задач моделирования, обработки волновых процессов и исследования пространственных форм представления информации. Важнейшее концептуальное отличие нашей парадигмы заключается в том, что некоторые базовые операторы (в частности, операторы типа Адамара) рассматриваются нами как преобразования, которые потенциально могут быть реализованы не только программной эмуляцией или отдельными аппаратными элементами, но и самой геометрией Сфирали. В разработанной архитектурной модели зеркально-антисимметричные витки и плавный S-переход Сфирали формируют пространственные условия для фазовых поворотов за счет движения волнового фронта. Возможность физической реализации таких геометрических преобразований является одним из направлений дальнейшей математической и экспериментальной проверки проекта.

This investigation focuses on the potential of this technique to surpass the limitations of existing geometric optimization methods and offers a promising pathway toward enhanced precision and speed.

The research investigates the impact of different entanglement parameters and transformation techniques on the circuit's behavior.

title: Title: Non-Standard Differential Geometry for Cryptographic Applications
abstract: The security of cryptographic systems is increasingly reliant on the mathematical foundations underpinning their algorithms. Differential geometry, traditionally used for understanding geometric properties of spaces, offers a novel approach to cryptography by incorporating self-encryption and dynamic key generation. This paper explores the development of a new non-standard differential geometry framework designed to create ultra-secure cryptographic primitives. We present a novel geometric structure, the "Self-Enforcing Geometry," which leverages inherent cryptographic properties to detect any tampering attempts, thereby ensuring the integrity of cryptographic operations. This approach distinguishes itself from existing methods by explicitly incorporating self-encryption and dynamic key generation, offering a fundamentally different security paradigm. The core mechanism involves constructing a geometric structure that is inherently resistant to manipulation, providing a robust foundation for advanced cryptographic applications. This work demonstrates the potential of this framework to significantly enhance the security of cryptographic systems.

This system addresses the limitations of traditional methods by offering a robust and automated approach to probability generation. The research explores the design and implementation of this framework, demonstrating its effectiveness through illustrative examples and preliminary analysis.

title: 基于自适应自适应学习的强化学习算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning algorithm, termed Adaptive Self-Adaptive Learning (ASAL), designed to enhance exploration and convergence speed. Traditional reinforcement learning algorithms frequently employ fixed learning rates, limiting the algorithm's ability to effectively navigate complex environments. ASAL dynamically adjusts the learning rate of its policy based on error feedback, allowing for more efficient exploration and improved convergence. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis and experimental validation to demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach. The core mechanism involves a novel error-weighted learning rate adaptation strategy. The paper's core claim is that ASAL significantly improves convergence speed and exploration efficiency compared to existing methods, particularly in environments with high variance.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to topological field theory (TFT) simulation, focusing on the development of an adaptive topology network. The proposed method offers a significant advancement in simulation capabilities, particularly when dealing with systems exhibiting complex, evolving dynamics.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum error correction code design based on information theory principles. title: Dynamic Variable Program Specification Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program verification that addresses the limitations of traditional static verification methods in the face of evolving program requirements and environments. The core idea is to construct a dynamic variable program specification verification system capable of adapting its verification strategies and models in real-time. This system leverages formal verification techniques to translate program specifications into formal models and integrates machine learning algorithms to dynamically adjust the verification strategy and the model itself. The system learns from verification results and adapts its approach to maintain accuracy and efficiency as the program's needs change. The primary contribution lies in providing a more flexible and adaptive verification mechanism, capable of handling the inherent dynamism of modern software development. We detail the system architecture, the formalization process, the machine learning component, and a conceptual framework for evaluating the system's performance. The system aims to improve verification coverage, reduce verification time, and ultimately enhance the reliability of software systems operating in dynamic environments.

title: Black Giant Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Giant Squirrels
abstract: This paper presents Black Giant Squirrel (BGS), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of giant squirrels. The algorithm mimics the squirrel's strategic selection of food sources, considering factors like food availability, distance, and potential reward. BGS combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a unique 'memory' mechanism to learn from past successful foraging decisions. The core of BGS lies in its 'Squirrel Search' operator, which dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance based on the perceived scarcity or abundance of resources. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BGS through a series of benchmark test functions, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions efficiently. The algorithm's performance is compared with established metaheuristic algorithms like PSO and Differential Evolution, highlighting BGS's advantages in certain problem landscapes. The key innovation is the incorporation of a squirrel's learned memory, impacting the search process. The algorithm's parameters are designed to reflect the adaptive nature of the squirrel's foraging strategy, leading to robust and efficient optimization performance. The evaluation demonstrates the potential of BGS as a viable alternative for complex optimization challenges.

title: Benguela Fruit Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BFB-MOA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Benguela Fruit Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BFB-MOA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Benguela fruit bat ( *Carollia fusca*). Fruit bats are renowned for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex environments. The algorithm leverages the bat's echolocation and flight patterns to develop a search mechanism that combines aspects of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a modified echolocation model to determine the position and velocity updates of candidate solutions, incorporating a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance based on environmental complexity. The BFB-MOA aims to improve upon existing metaheuristic algorithms by incorporating a more biologically-inspired approach, leading to potentially faster convergence and better solution quality for a variety of optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark test functions, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. This research contributes to the field of optimization by offering a new, biologically-motivated approach that may prove valuable in various applications.

title: Certification within a Declared Class: Four Corrections to the Acceptance Criterion of Note 13
abstract: Note 13 of this series specified a construction attaining state IV₂ together with a machine-checkable acceptance criterion for the run intended to test it. Four defects in that specification were established after deposit. The deposited text is not amendable; this note corrects it, and corrects it in one direction only. The corrections are four. The class of admissible rules must be declared by enumeration and not by a property: under a class declared by a property the uniqueness condition is decidable and identically false on every run that does not exhaust the admissible domain (Proposition 1). The acceptance parameter p_min — an assigned quantity inside a certifying procedure, by the note's own account — is replaced by a separating-set requirement computed from the class and the domain before the run (Propositions 2 and 3); and the fork by which failure to attain p_min was made both a refutation of the construction and a licence to repeat with an enlarged corpus is closed by fixing the number of permitted extensions at zero. Condition 5 is restated for a fold that returns a verdict and no confidence, the budget it places on consensus confidence having lost its referent. A small run is defined, with a lower bound on its corpus derived from the separating structure of the declared class, and with the notion of a partial certificate indexed to the conditions it actually discharges. No correction enlarges the set of runs that would count as certified. Three of the four defects are instances of one failure — an outcome settled by the specification rather than by the world — and the corrections are directed at restoring the run's capacity to fail.

title: 混沌几何场模拟与量子信息融合
abstract: 混沌几何场模拟是研究混沌现象的强大工具,而量子信息融合则旨在利用量子力学的特性来提升混沌模拟的精度和效率。本研究旨在构建一个动态的、高度可控的混沌几何场模拟,能够精确地捕捉量子纠缠在非线性几何结构中的影响,并利用这种理解来优化量子计算的实现。我们提出了一种"动态混沌"的概念,将混沌的几何性质与量子纠缠的非线性相互作用结合,并利用自适应的几何结构来引导纠缠的传播。本研究的核心论点是,通过这种方法,可以实现对量子纠缠在非线性几何结构中的更深刻的模拟,从而为量子计算的优化和发展提供新的途径。

title: Temporal Bayesian Networks with Causal Discovery
abstract: This research introduces a novel approach to temporal data analysis by integrating Temporal Bayesian Networks (TBNs) with causal discovery algorithms. Traditional TBNs primarily focus on modeling temporal dependencies without explicitly considering causal relationships. This limitation hinders their ability to accurately represent and interpret dynamic systems, particularly when causal influences are significant. The proposed method addresses this gap by leveraging Bayesian networks to represent temporal dependencies and employing a causal discovery algorithm to infer the underlying causal structure from observed time series data. The resulting Temporal Bayesian Networks with Causal Discovery (TBCDNs) provide a more robust and informative model of dynamic systems, allowing for the identification of causal influences and facilitating more accurate predictions. This work demonstrates the potential of TBCDNs for applications in various domains where understanding the temporal evolution of systems and their causal relationships is crucial. The core contributions lie in the integration of causal inference within a temporal modeling framework and the development of a methodology for learning causal structures from time series data. The resultant network structure is represented by a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where nodes represent variables and edges represent probabilistic dependencies, incorporating temporal constraints.

title: Causal Graph Embeddings for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) agents frequently exhibit poor generalization capabilities when faced with environments differing subtly from those encountered during training. This research investigates a novel approach – causal graph embeddings – aimed at addressing this limitation. The core idea involves explicitly modeling the causal relationships inherent within the RL environment as a graph. This graph embedding is then learned and utilized by the agent to guide its policy learning. We hypothesize that by understanding the underlying causal structure, the agent can better adapt to unseen environments, leading to improved generalization performance. The proposed method offers a distinct advantage over traditional RL techniques that rely solely on correlation, potentially enhancing robustness and reducing the reliance on extensive environment-specific training. The primary contribution is a framework for integrating causal reasoning into RL, opening new avenues for more intelligent and adaptable agents.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum spin-based optimization algorithm designed to enhance the performance of quantum computing algorithms. The core mechanism centers around utilizing the self-steering properties of quantum spin systems to guide the optimization process, resulting in more robust and efficient solutions compared to conventional algorithms. This work demonstrates the potential of this algorithm to address challenges in the design and implementation of quantum algorithms.

title: Atlantic Spiny Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Atlantic Spiny Rat" (ASR), inspired by the foraging strategies of the Atlantic spiny rat ( *Phylloturus barbatus*). These rats are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging behavior, particularly their ability to locate and exploit scarce resources across a complex landscape. The ASR algorithm mimics these behaviors by employing a combination of exploration and exploitation phases, utilizing a novel representation of the search space based on a 'resource map' and a 'movement strategy' informed by the rat's observed foraging patterns. The algorithm's core components include a dynamic probability distribution, a gradient-based movement mechanism, and a 'risk aversion' parameter that influences the exploration phase. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ASR through simulations on various benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The results indicate that ASR offers a robust and adaptable approach to solving complex optimization challenges.

title: Quantum Error Correction: Adaptive Topological Optimization
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical component of quantum information processing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum states. Traditional approaches often rely on static optimization techniques, which can be computationally expensive and may not effectively address the inherent complexities of quantum systems. This paper introduces an adaptive topological optimization algorithm designed to dynamically adjust quantum state configurations during error correction, aiming to minimize noise and enhance overall performance. We propose a novel method that leverages the principles of topological optimization to guide the evolution of quantum states, achieving a significant improvement in error correction efficiency compared to existing approaches. This work offers a promising pathway towards more robust and efficient quantum information processing.

title: Title: Non-Linear Feedback Loops in Parameter Optimization (NLFPO)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for parameter optimization, termed Non-Linear Feedback Loops in Parameter Optimization (NLFPO), which leverages dynamically adjusted model parameters to achieve self-correcting convergence. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with convergence, particularly when dealing with complex, non-linear systems. NLFPO addresses this challenge by incorporating a feedback loop that allows the model to iteratively refine its own parameters based on the outcomes of previous iterations. We present a theoretical foundation and initial implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in a specific, albeit simplified, scenario. The core mechanism focuses on creating a continuous feedback process that promotes self-adjustment, ultimately leading to optimal parameter values.

title: Quantum Error Correction Driven Distributed Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to distributed machine learning (DML) that leverages the inherent error correction capabilities of quantum error correction (QEC) codes. The core claim is that incorporating QEC can significantly enhance the robustness of DML systems, particularly in environments with noisy communication channels. The proposed mechanism involves designing a QEC code specifically tailored to protect the parameter updates within a distributed model. The feedback signals generated by the QEC code are then utilized to intelligently adjust the model parameters, mitigating the detrimental effects of noise. This contrasts with conventional DML methods that often struggle to cope with communication noise, offering a direct improvement in system resilience through the utilization of QEC's properties. The theoretical framework presented demonstrates the potential for achieving high accuracy even under challenging conditions, marking a significant advancement in the intersection of quantum computing and machine learning. The key aspects explored include code selection, decoding strategies, and the integration of the decoded updates into the distributed model. The paper culminates with a discussion of potential challenges and future research directions.

title: Spatiotemporal Causal Inference with Graph Transformers
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to spatiotemporal causal inference utilizing Graph Transformers. Traditional methods frequently encounter difficulties when dealing with complex and irregular spatiotemporal data patterns. This work addresses this limitation by leveraging the inherent capabilities of Graph Transformers – a sophisticated architecture designed for sequence modeling – to effectively capture both spatial and temporal dependencies within such datasets. The core mechanism involves constructing a graph representation of the spatiotemporal data and then processing it with a Graph Transformer. This allows for the identification of causal relationships that would be missed by conventional techniques. We demonstrate the potential of this combined approach through theoretical analysis and outline a framework for its implementation. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of graph representation learning and Transformer architectures for robust causal discovery in dynamic systems. The effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated through a conceptual framework and future research directions are explored.

title: Title: Algorithmic Quantum Bias Mitigation through Adaptive Error Correction
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements across diverse fields, but the inherent fragility of quantum systems necessitates rigorous error mitigation. Quantum bias, arising from imperfections in the hardware, poses a significant threat to accuracy. This paper introduces an algorithmic quantum bias mitigation strategy centered around a novel "Bias-Aware Correction Network." The core mechanism leverages a dynamically adjusted error correction strategy, intelligently adapting the correction applied to quantum states based on a learned model of quantum bias. We propose a framework for continuous bias assessment and correction, demonstrating a significant improvement in fidelity compared to static error correction methods. The resulting algorithm offers a pathway to robust and reliable quantum computations.

title: Quantum State Cryptography: Adaptive Key Management for Enhanced Security
abstract: Quantum State Cryptography (QSC) is a promising paradigm shift in cryptography, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to establish secure communication. This paper explores the design of a novel QSC algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Key Establishment," focusing on dynamic key adjustment based on input data. Traditional cryptographic systems rely on static keys, making them vulnerable to attacks leveraging information gained through observation or manipulation. Our proposed algorithm utilizes quantum state manipulation to create a robust key management system capable of dynamically adapting to changing data, significantly enhancing security. The core mechanism centers around creating and maintaining quantum states that evolve in response to the input, leading to a secure and resilient key establishment process. This paper details the algorithm's design, the underlying mathematical framework, and the potential implications for cryptographic security.

title: Predictive Hardware Verification using Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum simulation for predictive hardware verification. Traditional hardware verification methods often rely on classical simulations and emulation, which struggle to accurately capture the complexities of modern digital circuits, particularly when considering subtle quantum effects. Quantum simulation offers a fundamentally different approach by leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to directly model the behavior of the circuit at a fundamental level. We propose a framework where a quantum computer simulates the circuit, accounting for phenomena such as charge noise and quantum tunneling. The core claim is that this approach can significantly improve the accuracy of hardware prediction, allowing for the early detection of vulnerabilities and the optimization of performance before physical fabrication. This paper details the theoretical foundations, outlines a potential implementation strategy, and discusses the challenges and opportunities associated with this emerging technology. The key metric for success will be the ability to identify design flaws undetectable by conventional methods, ultimately leading to more robust and efficient hardware designs.

title: Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning for Sparse Data
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to relational reasoning designed specifically for sparse data. Traditional relational reasoning methods struggle with sparse datasets due to the computational expense of constructing and manipulating full adjacency matrices. We propose a quantum-inspired strategy, drawing inspiration from weak measurements in quantum mechanics, to efficiently estimate relationships within sparsely connected graphs. The core idea is to perform probabilistic measurements on nodes, capturing their connectivity information without the need for exhaustive matrix calculations. A Bayesian inference framework then integrates these probabilistic measurements to produce robust relational estimates. The methodology offers a significant improvement over conventional methods, particularly when dealing with datasets where the vast majority of connections are absent. The key contribution lies in the strategic application of probabilistic measurement, reducing computational complexity and enhancing the accuracy of relational inferences. The system is formulated as a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) process, leveraging the principles of weak measurement to derive a sampling strategy for the relational space.

title: ## The Mimicry Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Inspired by Capuchin Monkey Social Dynamics
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimicry Algorithm (MA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the observed social dynamics and mimicry behavior of capuchin monkeys. title: Non-Linear Geometry Structure Optimization Based Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to non-linear geometry structure optimization utilizing adaptive quantum algorithms. We propose a framework where quantum algorithms are employed to efficiently and effectively optimize complex geometric structures. The core mechanism revolves around leveraging quantum phenomena, specifically superposition and entanglement, to achieve enhanced optimization capabilities compared to traditional methods. This work addresses the limitations of existing algorithms by integrating quantum optimization techniques into a comprehensive optimization pipeline. The goal is to develop a robust and scalable method for modeling and optimizing intricate geometric configurations, ultimately aiming for improved performance in various geometric applications. This paper will detail the design of the algorithm, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: 基于自适应的分布式概率模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel distributed probabilistic model leveraging the inherent properties of probability spaces to improve prediction accuracy. Traditional probabilistic models often employ static parameters, limiting their ability to adapt to changing data. Our proposed model dynamically adjusts model parameters based on prediction feedback, enabling a more robust and accurate probabilistic forecasting process. The core mechanism centers around characterizing the probability space through self-attention mechanisms, allowing the model to intelligently refine its estimations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, highlighting its superior performance compared to existing methods. Keywords: Probabilistic Modeling, Distributed Systems, Self-Attention, Prediction Accuracy, Adaptive Learning.

title: PASM-Net: A Coordinate-Aware Manifold-Regularized Framework for Open-Set UAV RF Fingerprint Identification
abstract: To address the challenges of classifying known categories and rejecting unknown categories in the radio-frequency fingerprinting of uncooperative UAVs in open, low-altitude environments, this paper proposes PASM-Net, an open-set recognition method based on coordinate awareness and manifold continuity regularization. Existing deep learning-based RFFI methods still suffer from two shortcomings in open scenarios: First, while conventional convolutions and global pooling yield compact representations, they may weaken position-related information in the time–frequency spectrum, thereby affecting the model’s ability to characterize frequency-hopping trajectories and local time–frequency structures; on the other hand, decision mechanisms that rely solely on Softmax classifiers or simple distance metrics are susceptible to signal amplitude fluctuations and intra-class distribution dispersion, leading to the misclassification of unknown samples into known classes. To address these issues, this paper designs the PASM-Net feature-learning framework. First, the model employs multiscale hollow convolutions to extract local time–frequency features across different receptive fields and introduces a coordinate attention mechanism (Coordinate Attention, CoordAtt) prior to global pooling, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to represent position-related information in both the time and frequency domains. Second, the model introduces manifold continuity regularization (MCR) in the fused semantic space. By constraining feature variations within local neighborhoods via a Laplacian regularization term, MCR reduces the dispersion of known-class feature distributions. Finally, the model employs ArcFace to enhance the angular separability among known classes and performs open-set classification based on the cosine distance between test samples and the centers of known classes. The experimental results across six open-set scenarios on the DroneRFb-Spectra dataset showed that PASM-Net achieved an average true unknown rate (TUR) of 99.48%, an unknown accuracy of 97.9%, and an unknown-class precision (UP) of 87.3%, while maintaining a high performance in known-class recognition. Under the current experimental setup, this effectively improves the trade-off between known-class classification and unknown-class rejection.
