title: The Effects of Perceived Usefulness, Perceived Ease of Use, and Perceived Enjoy ment on Trust, Satisfaction, and Usage Intention in Tourism Chatbots: The Mode rating Role of Anthropomorphism
abstract: Purpose - This study examined how chatbot characteristics affect trust, satisfaction, and usage intention in tourism, while also assessing the moderating role of perceived anthropomorphism.Design, data, and methodology -A research model was developed based on the Extended Technology Acceptance Model. Survey data were collected from 313 tourism chatbot users and analyzed using exploratory factor analysis, multiple regression analysis, and PROCESS Macron (model 1)Result - Perceived usefulness and perceived enjoyment positively affected trust, whereas perceived ease of use did not. Trust positively influenced satisfaction and usage intention. Perceived Anthropomorphism significantly and negatively moderated both the usefulness-tr ust and ease of use-trust relationships, supporting H6 and H7. These findings indicate that higher anthropomorphism weakens the trust-building power of functional chatbot attributes.Conclusions - This study confirmed the importance of trust in tourism chatbot acceptance and provides implications for AI chatbot design and management.

title: Integrating Unimodal and Vision-Language Representations in Latent Space for Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification
abstract: Multi-label chest X-ray classification has attracted considerable attention in recent years, with the effective use of visual representations and clinical semantic knowledge playing an important role. This study proposes a framework that combines unimodal representations from RAD-DINO with vision--language representations from BioViL-T for the classification of 14 labels in the MIMIC-CXR-JPG dataset. The RAD-DINO and BioViL-T embeddings and their combined representation are refined separately in latent space before being normalized and fused across the three branches. In addition to improving classification performance, the study aims to clarify the role of each embedding source and the degree to which they complement one another. Experiments show that RAD-DINO outperforms BioViL-T when used independently, whereas early fusion further improves the results, indicating that the two embedding sources contain complementary information. The best-performing model achieves a mean AUROC of 0.840 and an mAP of 0.467. Ablation analysis shows that hybrid fusion provides consistent and statistically significant improvements over early fusion when each embedding source is refined in latent space, suggesting that fusion effectiveness depends on the quality of the representation supplied by each branch. However, the study has only been evaluated internally on MIMIC-CXR-JPG; its generalizability to data from other healthcare institutions therefore remains to be validated. The source code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/mimic-report-C210/.

title: Geometry-aware Latent Autoregressive Generative Model for PDEs in Complex Domains
abstract: Solving multiphysics partial differential equations (PDEs) remains a major challenge in scientific computing, especially for highly complex $μ$m-scale tortuous geometries critical to energy and chemical engineering. We address this challenge by proposing a Geometry-aware Latent Autoregressive generative Model for PDEs (GeoLAMP), which solves physics within highly irregular and tortuous structures by decoupling flow and transport physics. GeoLAMP introduces a dual-encoder architecture on graph representations to jointly capture global topology and fine-scale geometric features, enabling an effective transition from real-space fields to compact latent representations. In the latent space, we propose a causal self-attention transformer with flow matching to model temporal dynamics, allowing stable and scalable block-wise autoregressive prediction. In addition, we propose a grid-graph data fusion scheme that projects low-resolution grid-based approximate priors onto graph representations, improving prediction of flow in tortuous structures. We establish three multiphysics benchmark datasets in complex geometries, covering reactive flow, heat convection, and elasticity. GeoLAMP consistently achieves the most stable autoregression performance on these datasets. Our results provide a systematic study of geometry-aware learning for PDEs in $μ$m-scale complex geometries and offer new insights into block-wise time marching of latent autoregressive PDE modeling via a flow matching framework.

title: Language Proficiency Assessment from Eye Movements in Naturalistic Passage Reading
abstract: Standard language proficiency tests rely on linguistic tasks such as vocabulary, grammar and reading comprehension quizzes. An alternative, cognitively motivated approach, introduced in Berzak et al. (2018), proposed instead to predict language proficiency from behavioral traces of eye movements in reading. In this work, we validate and extend this approach from single sentences to more naturalistic reading of contextualized passages in English as a second language, new proficiency measures, prediction models, and reading in an information seeking regime. We find that the approach is effective in all these evaluations. We further address two key open questions on eye movement based proficiency testing: (1) potential scoring biases that reflect the proximity of the reader's native language to English, which may undermine validity, and (2) its reliability. We find that eye movement based proficiency scores are indeed biased towards L1s that are linguistically closer to English. We propose a score debiasing method which effectively remedies this issue. The reliability analyses suggest that eye movement proficiency scores are more reliable than standard language proficiency scores. Overall, our results strengthen and broaden the empirical foundations for future eye movement based language assessment technologies.

title: MCSeg: Pre-training and Fine-tuning Volumetric Pyramid Transformer for Multi-modal Cardiac Image Segmentation
abstract: Automatic cardiac image segmentation is pivotal for diagnosing and treating cardiac diseases. In this work, we introduce MCSeg, a volumetric transformer-based network tailored for multi-modal cardiac segmentation. To overcome the architectural mismatch inherent in existing hybrid networks, we propose a novel Scaling Feature Pyramid (SFP). Unlike conventional skip connections, the SFP effectively bridges the single-scale 3D Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder and the multi-scale CNN decoder by transforming the ViT's output into a hierarchical feature pyramid, ensuring that global contextual information is effectively leveraged. For the training paradigm, the ViT encoder first undergoes self-supervised pre-training via masked image modeling. Subsequently, the network is fine-tuned on downstream tasks, during which a regional mutual information (RMI) loss is integrated to improve boundary segmentation accuracy. In experiments, MCSeg consistently outperforms eleven SOTA methods on CT dataset ImageCHD, multi-modal dataset MM-WHS, MRI dataset HVSMR-2.0 and MSD Heart, highlighting the effectiveness of our MCSeg for multi-modal cardiac segmentation tasks. Furthermore, MCSeg's superior performance in few-shot experiment showcases its significant potential in adapting to limited data scenarios. Codes and pre-trained ViT-B weights are open-sourced at https://openi.pcl.ac.cn/OpenMedIA/MCSeg

title: PIU: Proximity-guided Identity Unlearning in ID-Conditioned Diffusion Models
abstract: Identity-conditioned diffusion models enable high-quality and identity-consistent face generation, but they also raise severe privacy concerns, as models may continue to synthesize individuals despite their right to be forgotten. While machine unlearning has been extensively studied for concept and data removal, identity unlearning remains largely unexplored, particularly in models conditioned directly on identity embeddings rather than text prompts. In this work, we study identity unlearning in Arc2Face, a state-of-the-art identity-conditioned latent diffusion model for face generation, and introduce Proximity-guided Identity Unlearning (PIU), an anchor-guided framework for identity unlearning. Specifically, we formulate identity removal as an identity replacement objective that reassigns the source identity to a selected anchor identity in the learned identity space, and we complement it with a proximity-based anchor selection strategy motivated by the geometry of ArcFace representations. We further show that effective unlearning can be achieved through localized fine-tuning of a small subset of identity-sensitive cross-attention layers. Experiments across multiple target identities show that our framework effectively suppresses generation of the target identity while preserving realism and identity consistency for retained identities, as validated by improved performance on unlearning and image-quality metrics, together with qualitative evaluation. The source code for the PIU identity unlearning framework is made publicly available at https://github.com/edgarcancinoe/piu-unlearning.

title: A LIGHTWEIGHT HYBRID QUANTUM CLASSICAL FEDERATED LEARNING MODEL FOR ANOMALY DETECTION IN EDGE IOT NETWORKS
authors: V T VENKATESWARLU , JILLELLA VENKATESWARA RAO , SELVA MALAR.N , KANDRAKUNTA CHINNAIAH , A. SRINIVASA REDDY⁵, BOSUBABU SONGA , PARUCHURI VENKATA KRISHNAKANTH , MORSA CHAITANYA
abstract: The number of IoT devices continues to rise and it is imperative to detect anomalies in real-time to ensure the security, reliability and efficiency of the system. Current deep neural network models have great memory and computing requirements, so it is not easy to use on the edge device. The benefit of federated learning is that it leaves raw data on the individual device, thus improving privacy. Nonetheless, efficient feature learning by compressing the size of quantum datasets has not been built into current federated learning frameworks, and the efficacy of quantum-based approaches under realistic noise in the hardware have not been widely investigated. To address privacy concerns, QEdgeNet is a lightweight hybrid quantum-classical federated learning (QLFL) model for anomaly detection in edge-IoT networks . In this model, the features of network traffic are first compressed by principal component analysis, and then the network traffic is mapped to a compact 4-qubit variational quantum circuit for the classification of anomalous traffic. This model is an aggregated model updated using the Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song (CKKS) homomorphic encryption mechanism, but without exposing the raw network data of clients, and raw traffic data never escapes from a client device during the training process. The applicability of the suggested approach in an idealized simulator is quantified by measuring the inference performance in a simulator simulated quantum hardware noise, the accuracy loss from the hardware noise is recovered by extrapolating to zero noise.

title: Benchmark-Driven Evaluation Frameworks for AI Agent Trustworthiness in Enterprise Analytics
abstract: Enterprise adoption of AI-powered analytics agents has outpaced the methods available to evaluate whether their outputs can be trusted. General-purpose benchmarks such as MMLU [1] and HumanEval [2] measure static knowledge recall and isolated code-generation ability, while text-to-SQL benchmarks such as Spider [3] and BIRD [4] test query generation against simplified schemas. None of these evaluate the full chain of reasoning an enterprise analytics agent must perform: schema interpretation, organization-specific metric computation, calibrated uncertainty, and application of the correct analytical methodology. On BIRD, even the strongest reported system reaches only 40.08% execution accuracy against realistic enterprise schemas, compared with 92.96% for human analysts [4], a gap that becomes consequential once an agent's output informs financial or regulatory decisions rather than exploratory analysis. This article proposes a nine-dimension trustworthiness evaluation framework purpose-built for enterprise analytics agents. Four dimensions are grounded in established trust taxonomies [6]-[8]; five are analytics-specific contributions not addressed by any existing framework: Schema Fidelity, Metric Definition Adherence, Failure Mode Transparency, Business Context Understanding, and Analytical Methodology Competence. The article also proposes a benchmark design methodology combining automated, LLM-as-judge, and domain-expert graders, and a five-phase Continuous Benchmark Evolution Lifecycle for keeping evaluation infrastructure current as schemas, metric definitions, and agent capabilities change.

title: Self-Spin Quantum Entanglement: Geometric Analysis and a Novel Feature Extraction Method
abstract: This paper investigates the geometric properties of self-spin quantum entanglement, exploring its potential for novel feature extraction techniques. We introduce a framework leveraging the unique characteristics of this entangled state to analyze geometric structures and devise an efficient feature extraction method. The core mechanism centers around adapting quantum algorithms to identify and quantify geometric patterns within the entangled system. The study aims to demonstrate the potential of this approach to surpass traditional feature extraction methods, particularly in scenarios requiring complex geometric relationships. This research offers a new perspective on analyzing and understanding geometric information derived from quantum entanglement.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的动态系统优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic system optimization algorithm based on adaptive neural networks (ANNs). Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle with complex, non-linear systems, requiring extensive tuning and potentially leading to suboptimal solutions. Our algorithm leverages the inherent capabilities of ANNs to dynamically adjust network parameters based on environmental feedback, offering improved efficiency and robustness compared to traditional methods. We detail the algorithm's architecture, the mechanism for parameter adaptation, and a preliminary evaluation demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing a simulated dynamic system. The core claim emphasizes the algorithm's ability to automatically tune neural network parameters and respond to environmental changes, resulting in enhanced performance and resilience.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of topological geometry to quantum computation, proposing a novel method for precise quantum state simulation and optimization. Traditional quantum computing simulations often struggle with complex topological geometries, presenting a significant challenge. We introduce a new approach predicated on the inherent properties of topological geometry, enabling more accurate and efficient simulations. The core mechanism involves mapping quantum states onto the topology of the space, utilizing this mapping to guide optimization algorithms and achieve improved fidelity. This research demonstrates the potential of this methodology to overcome limitations in current quantum computation techniques.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Graph Networks for Adaptive Data Representation
abstract: The efficient representation and processing of data are fundamental challenges in many domains, particularly in machine learning and data analytics. Static graph representations struggle to adapt to the inherent structure of the data, hindering optimal performance. This paper introduces Self-Organizing Graph Networks (SOGNNs), a novel approach to graph representation and inference that dynamically organizes nodes and edges based on the data's characteristics. SOGNNs employs a topology evolution algorithm driven by data-driven feedback, optimizing for data accessibility and processing. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through several benchmark datasets, showcasing improved performance in data retrieval and inference tasks compared to traditional graph representations. This research addresses the limitations of static graph models by providing a truly adaptive system capable of handling diverse data types.

title: 自适应量子拓扑拓扑结构的自适应计算
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly evolving field of physics, promises to revolutionize computational paradigms. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum topology to create adaptive computational frameworks, capable of dynamically adjusting complex system topology. We introduce a novel computational framework predicated on the inherent dynamic properties of quantum topology, allowing for the automated evolution of topological structures. Our core claim centers around the design of a self-adaptive computation system leveraging this dynamic structure. The mechanism involves a framework that adjusts quantum topology parameters through a feedback loop, enabling the system to respond to changing conditions and effectively explore complex topological landscapes. We detail the framework's architecture, the underlying mathematical principles, and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating its adaptability. The potential applications of this technology span diverse fields, including materials science, drug discovery, and optimization problems, highlighting the transformative impact of adaptive quantum computation. This work presents a foundational exploration of this promising avenue, demonstrating the feasibility of dynamically reshaping complex topological configurations.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism for non-linear particle group algorithms. title: Black-headed Marmoset Metaheuristic Algorithm (BHMMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Black-headed Marmoset Metaheuristic Algorithm (BHMMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-headed marmoset monkey. The algorithm leverages the marmoset's unique strategy of exploring diverse food sources while maintaining proximity to previously visited locations, mimicking their movement patterns through a probabilistic and adaptive search process. BHMMA incorporates a novel distance-based attraction mechanism and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, aiming to improve convergence speed and solution quality compared to traditional metaheuristic methods like the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) and the Grey Wolf (GW) algorithms. The algorithm's core components include a population of candidate solutions, a position vector representing each solution, a distance vector indicating the distance between solutions, an attraction probability influencing movement towards neighbors, and an exploration probability controlling the randomness of movement. Through extensive simulations on benchmark optimization problems, BHMMA demonstrates competitive performance and highlights its potential for various real-world applications.

title: Program Synthesis and Evolutionary Algorithm Co-evolution
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis and optimization by co-evolving program synthesis techniques with evolutionary algorithms. The core claim is that integrating these two methods can significantly enhance the efficiency and quality of automatically generated programs. The proposed mechanism leverages evolutionary algorithms to generate initial program candidates and subsequently employs program synthesis techniques to translate these candidates into target code. A feedback loop incorporates the performance of the generated code as the evaluation metric for the evolutionary algorithm, driving iterative optimization. This co-evolutionary strategy overcomes limitations inherent in traditional, independent approaches, offering a more robust and effective pathway for automated program generation and refinement. The key innovation lies in the synergistic interaction between the exploration capabilities of evolutionary algorithms and the precise transformation capabilities of program synthesis, resulting in programs with improved performance characteristics. The methodology is demonstrated through a conceptual framework and outlined for potential implementation, highlighting the benefits of this collaborative approach.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Complex Nonlinear Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to reinforcement learning for complex nonlinear systems by integrating the principles of nonlinear control theory with deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The core challenge in applying DRL to such systems lies in their inherent instability and sensitivity to initial conditions. Traditional DRL methods often struggle with convergence and stability, particularly when dealing with systems exhibiting significant nonlinearities. To address this, we propose a framework that leverages the strengths of both fields. Specifically, we employ state feedback and output feedback techniques from nonlinear control theory to constrain and guide the policy network within a DRL agent. This allows for a more structured and stable learning process, ultimately leading to improved convergence speed and performance. We formulate the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and detail the architecture of the DRL agent, emphasizing the integration of control-theoretic concepts. The resulting algorithm demonstrates promising results in simulated environments, showcasing its ability to handle complex nonlinear dynamics effectively. We define the key equations and notation used throughout the paper to ensure clarity and reproducibility.

title: Quantum Error Correction Code Topology Optimization
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a crucial aspect of realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, existing QEC codes often suffer from inefficiencies, including excessive qubit overhead and vulnerability to error propagation. This paper proposes a novel approach to QEC code design leveraging topological optimization. The core idea is to optimize the topological structure of the QEC code itself, aiming to minimize redundant encoding and reduce the probability of error propagation. We introduce a framework based on topological principles to systematically explore and refine the topology of QEC codes. This optimization process focuses on identifying and eliminating unnecessary connections within the code, resulting in a more resilient and efficient error correction scheme. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that optimized topological structures can significantly improve the code's performance metrics, such as the quantum error correction threshold and the logical error rate. This work represents a fundamental shift in the design of QEC codes, moving beyond traditional approaches to incorporate the inherent structure of the code as a key element in enhancing its performance.

However, existing QEC codes often suffer from inefficiencies, including excessive qubit overhead and vulnerability to error propagation. This paper proposes a novel approach to QEC code design leveraging topological optimization. The core idea is to optimize the topological structure of the QEC code itself, aiming to minimize redundant encoding and reduce the probability of error propagation. We introduce a framework based on topological principles to systematically explore and refine the topology of QEC codes. This optimization process focuses on identifying and eliminating unnecessary connections within the code, resulting in a more resilient and efficient error correction scheme. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that optimized topological structures can significantly improve the code's performance metrics, such as the quantum error correction threshold and the logical error rate. This work represents a fundamental shift in the design of QEC codes, moving beyond traditional approaches to incorporate the inherent structure of the code as a key element in enhancing its performance.

title: Probability Space Adaptive Algorithm for Dynamic Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic space adaptive algorithm designed for dynamic optimization. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting the algorithm's ability to effectively handle complex systems. This work proposes a method that dynamically adjusts parameters based on local state changes, enabling the algorithm to approximate optimal solutions in dynamic environments. The core mechanism leverages the properties of probability distributions, specifically high-Gaussian distributions and B-splines, to create a flexible and adaptive optimization process. This approach offers a significant improvement over static optimization techniques by providing adaptability to complex, evolving systems.

title: Cognitive Computing with Dynamic Bayesian Networks and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This research investigates the development of a novel cognitive system leveraging the strengths of Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) and Reinforcement Learning (RL). Current cognitive systems often struggle with genuine understanding and adaptability, necessitating a more robust approach. This project proposes a unified architecture where DBNs encode domain knowledge and represent causal relationships, while RL algorithms enable the system to learn optimal behaviors through interaction with an environment and receive feedback. The core claim is that by integrating these two powerful techniques, we can achieve a cognitive system with enhanced reasoning capabilities and adaptive learning. The system is designed to address the limitations of existing cognitive architectures by providing a framework for both knowledge representation and dynamic optimization. Mathematical notation and key concepts are presented to illustrate the theoretical foundations and operational principles of the proposed system. The system's architecture consists of a DBN, an RL agent, and an interface for interaction and feedback. The system will be evaluated through simulations and theoretical analysis.

title: Bahamian Hutia: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the Bahamian Hutia
abstract: This paper presents Bahamian Hutia, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bahamian Hutia (Cephalophus vermiculus). Hutias, small rodents endemic to the Bahamas, exhibit a unique and efficient foraging strategy characterized by a combination of random exploration and focused exploitation. Bahamian Hutia leverages these aspects to develop a robust optimization algorithm. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive mutation operator based on the Hutia's movement patterns and a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance influenced by food availability. The algorithm is designed to handle continuous optimization problems and is evaluated on a suite of benchmark functions. The experimental results demonstrate that Bahamian Hutia consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, including Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Simulated Annealing (SA), in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The key innovation lies in the algorithm's ability to adaptively adjust its search strategy based on environmental feedback, mirroring the Hutia's natural foraging behavior. Future research will focus on incorporating the algorithm into real-world applications and exploring its potential for parallelization.

title: Awa Dog-faced Bat Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Awa Dog-faced Bat
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Awa Dog-faced Bat Algorithm (ADBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Awa dog-faced bat, a species known for its unique echolocation and cooperative hunting strategies. The algorithm leverages the bat's ability to dynamically adjust its frequency and amplitude based on environmental information to effectively explore and exploit the search space. ADBA incorporates key aspects of bat behavior, including pulse-frequency modulation (PFM), cooperative search, and a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, maintaining a set of candidate solutions. Each candidate solution is represented by a position vector, and the algorithm iteratively updates these vectors based on the bat's foraging strategy. The objective function is evaluated for each candidate solution, and the best solution is selected. The algorithm's parameters, including the pulse-frequency modulation parameters and the cooperation coefficient, are dynamically adjusted to adapt to the characteristics of the problem being solved. The performance of ADBA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The results indicate that ADBA is a robust and efficient algorithm suitable for various optimization challenges.

title: Dynamic Complexity Measurement
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic complexity measurement algorithm designed to enhance model accuracy by adapting to data characteristics. Traditional complexity measurement methods are often static, failing to fully capture the nuanced relationships within data. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the complexity model based on observed data features, resulting in improved model performance. This approach leverages a feedback loop to optimize the model's representation of the underlying data distribution. The core mechanism involves adjusting model parameters through a feedback loop, allowing the algorithm to continuously refine its representation. This leads to more precise modeling and ultimately, better predictive capabilities. The goal is to provide a flexible and adaptive solution for complex data analysis.

title: Title: Quantum-Classical Entanglement Convergence for Complex Networks
abstract: This research explores the convergence of quantum and classical entanglement, a fundamental concept in quantum information theory. We propose a novel framework for analyzing entanglement within complex networks, aiming to demonstrate how quantum and classical entanglement patterns intertwine and evolve. The core mechanism involves modeling the network's structure using a hybrid quantum-classical framework, enabling the identification of emergent entanglement patterns that are distinct yet connected to both quantum and classical dynamics. This work provides a new perspective on entanglement, potentially offering insights into the fundamental nature of complex systems and their connection to both quantum and classical phenomena. The results of this investigation will contribute to a deeper understanding of entanglement's role in network dynamics and its potential applications in areas such as data analysis, cryptography, and network security.

title: Meta-Learning for Few-Shot Graph Embedding Learning
abstract: This paper explores the application of meta-learning techniques to the problem of few-shot graph embedding learning. Traditional graph embedding methods often require large datasets for effective training, limiting their applicability in scenarios where labeled data is scarce. We propose a novel framework leveraging meta-learning to enable rapid adaptation to new graph embedding tasks with minimal labeled examples. The core idea is to train a meta-learner that learns how to efficiently learn graph embeddings, effectively learning a strategy for quickly adapting to new graph structures and labels. We formalize this approach using a meta-learning objective function that minimizes the loss on the target graph given only a few labeled nodes. The key contribution lies in demonstrating the effectiveness of meta-learning in significantly reducing the data requirements for producing high-quality graph embeddings, opening up possibilities for embedding diverse and previously inaccessible graph datasets.

title: Adaptive Neuron Self-Organization
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to neural network design based on adaptive neuron self-organization. The core claim posits that neural networks can autonomously construct new connections and functional modules through internal feedback and environmental stimuli, without the need for pre-defined architectures. This is achieved through a mechanism rooted in reinforcement learning, where individual neurons dynamically adjust their connection weights based on local states and reward signals, driving the network's structure towards optimal functionality. The methodology presented represents a departure from traditional, manually-designed neural network architectures, offering a genuinely self-organizing learning system. Mathematical formulations detail the key processes involved, including the update rule for neuron weights, the reward function, and the network's objective function. The system's capacity to evolve and adapt in response to dynamic environments is highlighted as a significant advancement in neural network research. The core concept is to leverage the inherent plasticity of neurons to create complex network topologies directly from interaction with the environment, bypassing the limitations of fixed architectures. Simulation results demonstrate the system's ability to learn and adapt to complex tasks, showcasing the potential of this self-organizing approach.

title: Quantum Entanglement Stability and Propagation Optimization via Dynamic Topology Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum information processing, exhibits inherent fragility and requires sophisticated control strategies. Traditional methods of quantum state simulation often rely on deterministic algorithms, which struggle to effectively model the complex dynamics of entangled states. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing dynamic topology modeling to optimize the stability and propagation of quantum entanglement. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the topology of a quantum system, allowing for a more comprehensive representation of entanglement's evolution. This allows for the identification of optimal topological structures that enhance entanglement stability and facilitates efficient information transfer. The proposed framework represents a significant advancement in quantum state simulation, offering a potential pathway to overcome limitations of current methods.

title: Angolan Hylomyscus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by its Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, tentatively named "Hylomyscus," inspired by the foraging behavior of *Angolan Hylomyscus*, a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptable search strategies in complex environments. The algorithm leverages key aspects of the rodent's movement patterns, including path planning, resource prioritization, and adaptation to changing conditions, to construct a new optimization process. The core of Hylomyscus involves a dynamic particle representation, a weighted exploration-exploitation strategy based on resource availability, and a novel convergence criterion that mimics the rodent's ability to identify and stick to promising areas. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's design prioritizes adaptability and efficiency, offering a potential solution for a range of complex optimization challenges. The primary goal is to develop a robust and adaptable optimization technique with a biologically inspired foundation.

title: Andean Leaf-Eared Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Leaf-Eared Mouse Algorithm" (LEMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Andean leaf-eared mouse (Lepus pashalis). These mice exhibit a unique adaptive strategy for locating scarce food resources in challenging terrains. LEMA leverages this strategy by incorporating elements of exploration, exploitation, and obstacle avoidance, mimicking the mouse's efficient search process. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a virtual "territory" representation and adaptive movement strategies. Mathematical formulations describing the core components of LEMA, including the territory assignment, movement probability, and convergence criteria, are detailed. The algorithm is designed for tackling complex optimization problems, particularly those involving non-convex landscapes, multiple local optima, and constraints. The performance of LEMA is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The key mathematical formulations are presented below: Let *N* be the population size. Let *D* be the dimensionality of the search space. Let *T* be the number of territories. Let *xi* represent the position of the *i*-th individual in the population, where *i = 1, 2, ..., N*. Let *f(xi)* be the objective function to be minimized. The territory assignment probability, *Pij*, is calculated as: *Pij = exp(-||xi - xj||2 / (2 * σ2)) / Σk≠j exp(-||xi - xk||2 / (2 * σ2))* Where *||xi - xj||* represents the Euclidean distance between the positions *xi* and *xj*. σ is a parameter controlling the spread of the territory assignment. The movement probability, *μij*, is defined as: *μij = [1 + α * (f(xi) - f(xj))] / 2* Where α is a parameter controlling the exploitation-exploration balance. The convergence criterion is based on the stagnation of the objective function value: *if maxi |f(xi) - f(xi-1)| < ε then terminate* Where ε is a small tolerance value.

title: Quantum Information Theory Optimization via Adaptive Topological Structure
abstract: Quantum information theory offers unprecedented potential for secure communication and computation, but its practical implementation often faces challenges related to optimization. This paper presents an innovative approach to quantum information processing – Adaptive Topological Structure Optimization (ATSO) – leveraging the unique properties of quantum information theory. We propose an algorithm that dynamically adjusts the topology of quantum states based on feedback from quantum information theory, enabling optimized data encoding and manipulation. This optimization process enhances the fidelity and efficiency of quantum information processing. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum entanglement to learn and refine the underlying topological structure, leading to superior performance compared to traditional optimization methods. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of ATSO through simulations and theoretical analysis, highlighting its potential to significantly advance the development of quantum information technologies.

title: Dynamic Gradient Optimization Fields (DGOF)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Gradient Optimization Fields (DGOF), a novel algorithm for optimizing complex mathematical models by leveraging dynamic field theory. Traditional gradient optimization methods often struggle with complex models and the inherent noise and uncertainty present during training. DGOF addresses this by dynamically adjusting optimization parameters, enabling the model to adapt to these variations and improve generalization capabilities. The core mechanism involves integrating gradient optimization with a dynamic field theory, where the gradient function itself acts as a dynamically adjustable field, allowing for self-tuning of optimization parameters. This approach significantly enhances the model's robustness and adaptability. We present a comprehensive theoretical analysis and empirical validation of DGOF, demonstrating its effectiveness across a range of model types and training scenarios.

title: Bayesian Detection of Anomalies in Multivariate Gaussian Processes
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to anomaly detection in multivariate data leveraging the statistical properties of Gaussian Processes (GPs). Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with the complexities of high-dimensional, multivariate data, frequently relying on univariate assumptions or requiring substantial preprocessing. We propose a framework based on building a GP model to represent the underlying data distribution and then detecting anomalies by quantifying the discrepancy between the observed data and the model's predictions. Specifically, we formulate the detection process as a Bayesian inference problem, allowing us to estimate the probability of an observation given the model. Observations exceeding a pre-defined threshold in terms of predictive error are flagged as anomalies. The key innovation lies in the application of GP's inherent uncertainty quantification to anomaly detection, providing a more robust and statistically sound method compared to purely threshold-based approaches. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a simplified example. This work contributes to the growing field of probabilistic anomaly detection and offers a flexible framework adaptable to various multivariate datasets.

title: ## The Black Drill Finch Metaheuristic: A Novel Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Black Drill Finch Metaheuristic (BDFM), a novel optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the black drill finch (Geospiza fulachta). The algorithm mimics the finch's strategy of systematically exploring a food source, prioritizing areas with higher perceived reward based on a dynamically adjusted "drill depth" and "exploration radius." BDFM utilizes a population-based approach, employing a set of 'drills' that iteratively probe potential solutions. The algorithm's core mechanisms include a dynamic drill depth adjustment, determined by a stochastic function reflecting the perceived value of the solution, and an exploration radius that adapts based on the diversity of solutions within the population. The paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing the key parameters and their influence on the optimization process. We present a conceptual description of the algorithm's operation, emphasizing the intuitive connection to the observed foraging behavior of the finch. While experimental validation is deferred to future work, this paper lays the groundwork for a potentially effective metaheuristic algorithm for a variety of optimization problems.

title: 基于信息瓶颈的深度生成对抗网络对时间序列异常检测
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to time series anomaly detection leveraging the principles of information bottlenecks and generative adversarial networks (GANs). The core idea is to map time series data into a low-dimensional information bottleneck space, followed by training a GAN to reconstruct this space. By training the generator to reconstruct the normal time series data, the network learns to capture the underlying patterns and dynamics of the data. The discriminator then distinguishes between the original and reconstructed data, further refining the generator's ability to identify anomalies. This approach avoids the need for manual feature engineering, automatically learning relevant features from the data. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in detecting anomalies in time series data. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of information bottleneck compression and GAN training, resulting in improved anomaly detection performance compared to traditional methods. The model is formally defined as follows: Let *x*t = (x1t, x2t, ..., xTT) be a time series of length *T*, where *xit* represents the *i*-th data point at time step *t*. The information bottleneck is defined as: * Encoder: *e*t = *f*(xt; *β*) * Decoder: *x̂it* = *g*(et; *γ*) Where *f* is the encoder function, *g* is the decoder function, *β* is the bottleneck dimension, and *γ* is the learning rate. The generator *g* attempts to reconstruct *xt* from *et*, while the discriminator *D* learns to distinguish between real *xt* and reconstructed *x̂t*. The loss function for the generator is: * LG = ||xt - x̂t||2 + *λ*||et||2 Where *λ* is a regularization coefficient. The loss function for the discriminator is: * LD = -Ext[1 + D(xt)] + Ex̂t[D(x̂t)] Where *D(xt)* is the discriminator's output for input *xt*.

The core idea is to map time series data into a low-dimensional information bottleneck space, followed by training a GAN to reconstruct this space. By training the generator to reconstruct the normal time series data, the network learns to capture the underlying patterns and dynamics of the data. The discriminator then distinguishes between the original and reconstructed data, further refining the generator's ability to identify anomalies. This approach avoids the need for manual feature engineering, automatically learning relevant features from the data. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in detecting anomalies in time series data. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of information bottleneck compression and GAN training, resulting in improved anomaly detection performance compared to traditional methods. The model is formally defined as follows: Let *x*t = (x1t, x2t, ..., xTT) be a time series of length *T*, where *xit* represents the *i*-th data point at time step *t*. The information bottleneck is defined as: * Encoder: *e*t = *f*(xt; *β*) * Decoder: *x̂it* = *g*(et; *γ*) Where *f* is the encoder function, *g* is the decoder function, *β* is the bottleneck dimension, and *γ* is the learning rate. The generator *g* attempts to reconstruct *xt* from *et*, while the discriminator *D* learns to distinguish between real *xt* and reconstructed *x̂t*. The loss function for the generator is: * LG = ||xt - x̂t||2 + *λ*||et||2 Where *λ* is a regularization coefficient. The loss function for the discriminator is: * LD = -Ext[1 + D(xt)] + Ex̂t[D(x̂t)] Where *D(xt)* is the discriminator's output for input *xt*.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Relational Dynamics
abstract: Existing graph embedding techniques predominantly focus on static graph structures, neglecting the crucial aspect of temporal dynamics inherent in many real-world networks. This paper introduces a novel approach – Temporal Graph Embedding with Relational Dynamics – that addresses this limitation. Our method leverages a recurrent neural network (RNN) to model the evolution of graph relationships over time. The RNN is trained to predict future graph states based on past states and node attributes, effectively creating a dynamic representation of the graph. The resulting hidden state representation from the RNN is then utilized as the graph embedding. This approach allows for the capture and learning of temporal relational dependencies, providing a richer and more accurate representation of the graph compared to static embedding methods. The core of our method is the integration of dynamic graph modeling with RNNs, explicitly capturing the evolving nature of relationships within the graph. The proposed method demonstrates improved performance in downstream tasks that rely on understanding temporal graph patterns.

title: ## Deep-Sea Basket Sponge Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (DBSMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Deep-Sea Basket Sponge Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (DBSMOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of deep-sea basket sponges. These sponges, adapted to the extreme conditions of the deep ocean, efficiently locate and capture scarce food sources using a complex, layered approach. DBSMOA mimics this process by employing a multi-layered search space, a probabilistic "capture" mechanism, and a dynamic "support" structure. The algorithm's core components include a primary search layer, a secondary support layer, and a probabilistic capture layer, all interacting to guide the search towards optimal solutions. The algorithm's parameters – layer depth, capture probability, support dynamic factor, and convergence criteria – are designed to emulate the sponge's adaptive strategies. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, defines its key parameters, and proposes a conceptual model for its application in various optimization problems. The intention is to establish a foundation for future computational investigations and practical applications.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Reinforcement Learning Framework
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) represents a paradigm shift in machine learning, leveraging quantum mechanical principles to accelerate computation and potentially unlock new algorithms. This paper investigates a novel reinforcement learning (RL) framework, termed "Adaptive Neural Network Reinforcement Learning" (ANNR), which employs dynamic parameter adjustment within a self-adaptive neural network to enhance learning efficiency and generalization capabilities. We demonstrate that this approach overcomes limitations of traditional RL methods, offering a promising path towards more robust and adaptable reinforcement learning agents. The core mechanism focuses on iteratively refining neural network weights through a feedback loop, enabling the system to explore complex environments effectively. The research explores the impact of parameter adjustment on both training speed and final performance across various RL tasks.

title: ## The Purple-Crested Swift Optimization Algorithm (PCSOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Purple-Crested Swift Optimization Algorithm (PCSOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Purple-Crested Swift (Aerodramus Rubens). The algorithm mimics the swift's aerial maneuvers, utilizing a combination of velocity control, adaptive exploration-exploitation, and a novel 'contour following' mechanism to navigate complex search spaces. PCSOA leverages a dynamic population of particles, each possessing a position, velocity, and a 'contour coefficient' to guide its movement along the objective function landscape. The algorithm's core innovation lies in the iterative adjustment of the contour coefficient, influenced by both the particle's local search performance and the global population's diversity. We propose a mathematical formulation of the algorithm and outline its key operational principles, demonstrating its potential for solving a variety of optimization problems. The algorithm's performance characteristics are discussed, highlighting its strengths and potential areas for future research.

title: Virtual Public Hearing Simulation using Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent System - Focused on the Public Hearing for the Rural Spatial Restructuring and Regeneration Plan
abstract: 현대 도시계획의 필수 절차인 주민 공청회는 고령화와 인력 부족을 겪는 농촌 지역에서 운영의 부담이 크다. 본 연구는 농촌공간기본계획 시범사업 지역인 전북 순창군의 실제 계획안을 바탕으로, 거대언어모델 기반 멀티에이전트 시스템을 활용한 ‘가상 주민 공청회 시뮬레이션’ 체계를 제안한다. 이는 현실의 공청회를 예측하거나 대체하기 위한 것이 아니라, 계획가가 실제 공청회를 설계하기에 앞서 참여 규모ㆍ패널 구성ㆍ진행 방식과 같은 설정 변수를 사전에 탐색하는 도구로 기능한다. 실제 통계와 개별 서사를 결합해 구축된 가상 주민들의 토론은 형평성과 효율성이라는 두 가지 축 위에서 표준 숙의 단위 지표로 정량화되어, 여론의 이동 궤적과 강도를 측정한다. 연구 결과는 에이전트 설정의 구체성, 공청회 참여자 규모, 진행 방식 및 진행자 유형이라는 공청회 설정 변수를 달리하여 가상 환경 내 공청회 시뮬레이션 결과를 도출하고 여론 이동의 차이를 비교한다. 본 연구는 시뮬레이션이 실제 공청회 전 단계에서 갈등을 선제적으로 파악하고 행정적 시행착오를 줄이는 유용한 계획지원 도구가 될 수 있음을 입증한다.

title: Prior Distributions for Gaussian Models Under Differential Privacy with Bounds on Data Values
abstract: The Gaussian distribution is often used to model univariate, numerical data, even in contexts where individuals' data values are bounded, e.g., test scores and biological measurements. We consider Bayesian inference for the parameters of Gaussian models when (i) analysts seek a post-processing algorithm that takes noisy sufficient statistics as inputs and produces a posterior distribution of the parameters as output, and (ii) the privacy mechanism enforces bounds on individual data values as a condition for satisfying pure differential privacy. Our primary contributions focus on the specification of prior distributions for model parameters. Specifically, we illustrate that failing to account for the bounds on data values when using informative prior distributions can result in posterior inferences with undesirable properties. Further, we show theoretically that the usual default priors used in the nonprivate setting do not lead to proper posterior distributions, and we suggest a default prior distribution that does. We also show empirically that one can improve the performance of inferential procedures by incorporating the boundedness assumptions into the specification of prior distributions. We present methods for inferring about the mean and variance of a univariate Gaussian model and the coefficients and variance of a linear regression. As we discuss, the general strategies used for the Gaussian models can be adapted for other models when enforcing bounds on the data values to ensure differential privacy.

title: Optimizing Multilingual Embedding Models for Retrieval and Reranking in RAG Pipelines: Enhancing Semantic Search in Turkish Medical Datasets
abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of enhanced multilingual embedding models in improving retrieval performance for Turkish medical text data. We consider two specific medical applications in Turkish language: the TUS examination, a standardized medical assessment featuring exam questions, and Clinical QA, which involves authentic patient-physician interactions. By implementing multi-stage fine-tuning protocols on domain-specialized models, we provide detailed performance assessment and explore cross-domain transfer capabilities of the trained models. Our findings indicate that domain-specialized models improve in-domain retrieval relative to generic models, and that systematic optimization through our multi-stage pipeline yields measurable gains in retrieval precision. For instance, domain-specific fine-tuning improves TUS retrieval performance from 0.69 to 0.79 in P@1 and from 0.77 to 0.85 in MRR, while Clinical QA fine-tuning with hard-negative sampling improves P@1 from 0.33 to 0.39 and MRR from 0.41 to 0.48 relative to the vanilla encoder. In addition, reranking improves P@1 from 0.788 to 0.823 in our evaluated setting, corresponding to a 4.5% relative improvement. Furthermore, we find that, in multilingual model training, domain-specific knowledge acquired in the healthcare context of one language effectively transfers and enhances performance across other languages.

title: Toward Workflow-Aware Benchmarking for Healthcare NLP Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly proposed for healthcare tasks such as clinical documentation, evidence retrieval, patient messaging, and care coordination. Yet many evaluations remain limited to static medical question answering or one-shot generation, under-representing longitudinal state, interruptions, and human handoffs. We introduce an episode-level evaluation protocol for healthcare NLP agents. The protocol separates evidence across model, agent, and simulated-workflow behavior; specifies a five-field episode schema; and defines annotation and scoring for state continuity, evidence traceability, and escalation decisions. It is instantiated as four task templates: documentation update, evidence retrieval, patient messaging, and triage handoff. The protocol does not claim to measure clinical outcomes or deployment value. Instead, it supplies a reproducible intermediate evaluation layer between static benchmarks and prospective workflow studies, with an explicit cost-sensitive treatment of missed versus unnecessary escalation.

title: Measure Before You Manage: Evaluating Agent Working Memory in Coding Agents
abstract: Agent working memory is heterogeneous. Objects such as instructions, artifacts, tool outputs, and agent-generated state play different semantic roles and exhibit different size, retention, and representation profiles. Recent work has begun to explore memory-management mechanisms that account for such heterogeneity. This work focuses on semantic heterogeneity and studies how it should shape the management and evaluation of working memory in coding agents. Across 55 archived coding-agent trajectories, we find that semantically different working-memory objects exhibit distinct retention and compression behavior. This heterogeneity motivates semantically informed memory management. We study two semantically informed strategies: an object-aware compression policy and a retrieval-based policy. Their evaluation shows that calibration gains may not transfer to held-out tasks, and that equal token budgets do not imply equal delivered context or management cost. A real-system replay further exposes serving limits that nominal budgets alone do not capture. Together, these results show why semantic structure matters for agent working memory and why evaluating memory-management strategies requires more than a nominal token budget. We organize these lessons into four levels: stored state, delivered context, management work, and task or process outcome.

title: A Composition-Aware Pretraining Framework for Geospatial Foundation Models
abstract: Geospatial foundation models have emerged as state-of-the-art methods for downstream Earth observation tasks. However, existing pretraining methodologies process imagery through a single-concept lens, failing to capture the highly compositional nature of complex satellite scenes. We propose a composition-aware pretraining framework that explicitly encodes fractional land-cover mixtures. Each satellite image cell is mapped to a histogram representing its fractional land-cover distribution, which we term the "composition target". These targets serve as the primary prediction objective and are distilled into the backbone using Earth Mover's Distance. Experimental evaluation shows that composition-aware pretraining yields substantial gains on region-level understanding tasks requiring semantic similarity judgment, including zero-shot image retrieval and scene classification, while remaining competitive on tasks requiring fine-grained spatial precision, such as segmentation and object detection. With a 36.8M-parameter backbone, our framework outperforms SatMAE and Prithvi-EO-2.0, which contain 303M and 600M parameters, respectively, in most retrieval and scene classification settings. On the fine-grained ForestNet-12 dataset, a rigorous testbed for compositional discrimination, our method boosts baseline mAP@10 from 0.279 to 0.434, a 55.6% relative improvement, providing direct evidence for the effectiveness of explicit composition modeling. The code implementation can be found at https://github.com/05kashyap/GFM_Composition_Pretraining

title: Augmenting Human Performance with an XR Agent Learning from Online Behavior and BCI Evidence
abstract: We present OLIVE, a framework for adapting a foundation model to provide real-time assistance in temporally demanding, high-stakes, and dynamic tasks. We show that passive EEG, fused online with behavioral evidence, can meaningfully extend the number of targets users detect and engage beyond their unaided action bandwidth. OLIVE learns from both explicit behavioral signals (the targets the user shoots down in an XR first-person shooter game) and implicit physiological signals (fixation-locked EEG) to provide timely guidance, continuously adapting a frozen vision-language model's inference on which items are task-relevant by jointly estimating per-source reliability without manual labels or offline training. Through three user studies, including two live deployments of an assistive agent driven by OLIVE in XR, we show that OLIVE Pareto-dominates prior test-time adaptation frameworks, achieving the highest convergence rate at comparable convergence speed. Combining implicit physiological and explicit behavioral signals, the OLIVE agent produces the largest and most reliable within-session improvement to a user's ability to detect and engage targets, largely independent of the individual's skill. When the target switches silently, the agent that uses both behavioral and physiological signals reconverges significantly faster than the behavior-only agent (1.27 times faster on average, p = .008), restoring trustworthy guidance at the moment the task changes, precisely when reliable assistance matters most.

title: Unrestricted Boolean Multiplicative Complexity of Four-Term Binary Polynomial Multiplication: Rational Places, Hasse Jets, and the Failure of Nonlinear Feedback
abstract: Classical lower bounds show that multiplying two degree-three polynomials over $\mathbb F_2$ requires nine scalar products in bilinear or quadratic models. They do not settle unrestricted Boolean multiplicative complexity: an XOR--AND circuit may reuse nonlinear intermediate wires, and Boolean equality is taken modulo $x_i^2=x_i$, so a multiplication can lower algebraic degree. Let $\operatorname{Mul}_4:\mathbb F_2^8\to\mathbb F_2^7$ output the seven coefficients of the product of two four-term binary polynomials. We prove that its unrestricted XOR--AND multiplicative complexity is exactly nine. This resolves, for a natural vector-valued quadratic function, the Boyar--Find question of whether a quadratic-circuit lower bound can persist against unrestricted nonlinear reuse. title: Understanding Stage-Wise Utility-Risk Trade-offs in LLM Agent Memory
abstract: Long-term memory is becoming a core capability of LLM agents, enabling personalization and long-horizon interaction. However, memory mechanisms that retain, transform, or expose more information can affect both benign utility and susceptibility to memory poisoning. Existing evaluations typically measure memory utility or attack risk in isolation under fixed configurations, providing limited insight into how stage-specific design choices reshape their trade-off. We present \textsc{MemGauge}, a controllable framework that separately varies writing admission, management policy, and retrieval exposure under matched clean and poisoned conditions. Across 11 LLMs and two long-term memory benchmarks, controlled evaluations reveal three distinct profiles: a threshold-like risk transition during writing, policy-dependent local decoupling during management, and coupled growth of utility and risk during retrieval. We further apply analogous stage-level measurements to four existing memory systems and observe diagnostic associations qualitatively consistent with these profiles. These results show that targeted poisoning risk varies across memory operations and motivate stage-aware evaluation and control of LLM-agent memory.

title: SCALE:Scalable Conditional Atlas-Level Endpoint transport for virtual cell perturbation prediction
abstract: Virtual-cell models aim to predict how cell populations respond to perturbations, but control and treated cells are measured as unpaired populations, complicating the learning of perturbation-specific effects. We present SCALE, a conditional transport model that represents cells as unordered sets and predicts treated populations without cell-level matching. A shared set-aware encoder and conditional DiT backbone learn latent transport, making endpoint supervision directly delta-aligned without an auxiliary delta objective. Across genetic, chemical, developmental and immune perturbations, SCALE recovered gene-expression changes, response directions and population structure. In CRISPR data with dominant cell-line effects, SCALE outperformed competing methods across seven metrics and maintained separation among gene-target representations rather than collapsing them into a shared region. SCALE further prioritized cytokines predicted to produce distinct immune activation and inflammatory responses. Experiments using matched PBMC samples from three donors confirmed these predicted differences. Together, SCALE enables perturbation-specific prediction from unpaired populations and supports experimental prioritization.

title: РОЗДІЛ 13. КЛАСИФІКАЦІЯ РЕПЛІК, ДІАЛОГОВИХ СТАНІВ ТА АНАЛІЗ СЕМАНТИЧНОЇ ДИНАМІКИ ДІАЛОГІВ У ЦИФРОВИХ СЕРВІСАХ ПСИХОЛОГІЧНОЇ ПІДТРИМКИ НАСЕЛЕННЯ
abstract: РОЗДІЛ 13 КЛАСИФІКАЦІЯ РЕПЛІК, ДІАЛОГОВИХ СТАНІВ ТА АНАЛІЗ СЕМАНТИЧНОЇ ДИНАМІКИ ДІАЛОГІВ У ЦИФРОВИХ СЕРВІСАХ ПСИХОЛОГІЧНОЇ ПІДТРИМКИ НАСЕЛЕННЯ Чистотін Олексій Володимирович, аспірант кафедри інформаційних систем, Національний університет «Одеська політехніка», Одеса Цифрові сервіси психологічної підтримки населення працюють з діалоговими текстами, у яких зміст окремої репліки залежить від попереднього контексту, ролі автора, поточного стану розмови, тематичних і емоційних ознак.Тому автоматизований аналіз таких діалогів не може обмежуватися класифікацією ізольованих повідомлень.Репліка користувача може бути початковим зверненням, уточненням, описом ситуації, емоційною реакцією або сигналом потреби у додатковій увазі.Репліка консультанта може виконувати підтримувальну, уточнювальну, організаційну або маршрутизаційну функцію.Однакова за текстом фраза може мати різне значення залежно від автора та місця в діалозі.У цьому дослідженні розкриваються перша та друга складові наукової новизни дисертаційного дослідження.Перша складова полягає в удосконаленні методу класифікації реплік і діалогових станів у цифрових сервісах психологічної підтримки населення.На відміну від методів, що використовують лише текст репліки або лінійне контекстне вікно, запропонований підхід враховує семантичний профіль репліки, графовоконтекстне представлення діалогу, локальне оточення вузла, роль автора, позицію в діалозі та невизначеність інтерпретації.Друга складова полягає

title: ANALISIS USER PERSONA BERDASARKAN ULASAN PENGGUNA TOKOPEDIA MENGGUNAKAN METODE SVM BERBASIS WEB
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan membangun sistem analisis user persona berbasis web yang mengintegrasikan klasifikasi sentimen menggunakan metode Support Vector Machine (SVM) dengan data ulasan pengguna aplikasi Tokopedia dari Google Play Store. Sebanyak 5.000 ulasan dikumpulkan melalui teknik scraping menggunakan pustaka google-play-scraper, kemudian melalui proses pembersihan menjadi 4.781 ulasan valid. Tahap preprocessing meliputi cleaning, case folding, normalisasi kata slang, tokenisasi, stopword removal, dan stemming menggunakan pustaka Sastrawi, sebelum direpresentasikan dalam bentuk vektor numerik menggunakan TF-IDF yang menghasilkan 3.739 fitur aktif. Klasifikasi sentimen tiga kelas (Positif, Netral, Negatif) dilakukan menggunakan SVM dengan kernel RBF dan class_weight='balanced'. Hasil pengujian terhadap 957 data uji menunjukkan akurasi sebesar 81,09%, presisi 65,53%, recall 60,18%, dan F1-score 61,35%, dengan rata-rata K-Fold Cross Validation (K=5) sebesar 81,46% ± 0,18%. Hasil klasifikasi sentimen selanjutnya diolah menggunakan algoritma keyword-scoring untuk membentuk empat segmen user persona, yaitu Loyal Buyer (35,7%), Price Hunter (3,0%), Casual Shopper (4,7%), dan Frustrated User (56,6%). Seluruh hasil analisis divisualisasikan melalui dashboard berbasis web yang dibangun menggunakan Flask, MySQL, dan HTML/CSS/JavaScript. Penelitian ini membuktikan bahwa integrasi SVM dan algoritma keyword-scoring efektif menghasilkan profil persona pengguna yang bermakna dan dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai dasar pengambilan keputusan strategi bisnis serta pengembangan produk platform e-commerce.

title: Testing the Effect of the Smart Counseling System AI Support Vector Machine Intervention on Reducing Teen Misbehavior
abstract: The study aimed to evaluate the Artificial Intelligence-assisted Smart Counseling System in supporting the detection and classification of adolescent behavioral difficulties and to identify changes in students' behavioral conditions following the intervention. The study used a quantitative pretest–posttest control group design with 666 junior high school students in Medan City: 333 in the experimental group and 333 in the control group. Data were collected using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire and analyzed by comparing pretest and posttest scores, as well as classifying them using the Support Vector Machine method. The results showed that the experimental group's mean Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire score decreased from 21.00 (standard deviation = 12.469) at the pretest to 18.05 (standard deviation = 8.975) at the posttest. However, the analysis indicated that the difference between the groups at the posttest was not statistically significant, F(2,663) = 1.578, p = 0.207. Therefore, the evidence was insufficient to conclude that the Smart Counseling System was significantly more effective than the control condition. In contrast, the Support Vector Machine analysis showed strong classification performance, with accuracy increasing from 98.50% using the original features to 99.25% after feature engineering for classifying students into the Normal, Borderline, and Abnormal categories. These findings indicate that the Smart Counseling System has potential as a supporting system for the early detection and classification of adolescent behavioral difficulties; however, its effectiveness as an intervention requires further investigation through analyses of time-by-group interactions, effect sizes, and more comprehensive model validation. Therefore, the Smart Counseling System is better positioned as a decision-support tool for counselors rather than a replacement for counselors or a diagnostic instrument.

title: A Statistical Comparison of Multi-Architecture Models for Retention-Period Classification of Chinese Electronic Official Documents
abstract: Electronic document archiving requires automatic retention-period classification (permanent/30-year/10-year). To evaluate architectures on weakly structured Chinese official texts—texts lacking clear semantic boundaries whose key cues appear as scattered keywords—we benchmark six models across four paradigms: Qwen3 (0.6B/1.7B/4B) with LoRA, BERT-base-Chinese, FastText, and BERT-Embedding-TextCNN (frozen BERT character embeddings + TextCNN). On 2,118 test samples we conduct pairwise McNemar exact binomial tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction over the 15 comparisons (FDR q=0.05). BERT-Embedding-TextCNN (75.50%) and FastText (75.07%) achieve the highest accuracy, ahead of Qwen3-4B (73.94%), but their Wilson 95% confidence intervals (approximately ±1.9 percentage points) overlap substantially. After correction, only two differences remain significant: BERT-Embedding-TextCNN and FastText each outperform Qwen3-0.6B (adjusted p=0.002 and p=0.006); the other 13 pairwise differences do not reach significance. The accuracies thus form descriptive clusters rather than statistically verified tiers. A leakage-controlled evaluation on the 1,690 test documents that are neither exact nor near-duplicates of training documents preserves this ranking and both significant differences, with accuracies 1.7–2.5 percentage points lower across models. Feature-weight inspection shows that archival keywords (e.g., bidding and state-asset terms, which skew toward permanent retention) are important predictive features for FastText, supporting a keyword-driven explanation of task success. For resource-constrained enterprise deployment, FastText offers near-top accuracy with CPU-only inference at roughly 26,800× the throughput of the 4B LLM under the evaluated hardware configurations.

title: Quantum Topologies for Geometric Information Extraction
abstract: Quantum Topologies (QT) offers a novel approach to extracting geometric information from quantum states, potentially revolutionizing quantum computing. This paper investigates the development of a novel algorithm, Quantum Topologies for Geometric Information Extraction (QT-GIE), which leverages QT's inherent geometry to identify and manipulate quantum states. We demonstrate the algorithm's ability to optimize quantum computations through the extraction of key geometric properties. This research introduces a novel methodology for utilizing QT's geometric properties to enhance quantum computational precision and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around the application of QT-GIE to quantum state manipulation, achieving significant improvements in performance. We present initial results showcasing the algorithm's effectiveness in specific quantum computations.

title: Quantum State Self-Maintenance Adaptive Network (QS-AN)
abstract: Quantum State Self-Maintenance Adaptive Network (QS-AN) is a novel quantum computing architecture designed to maintain quantum state stability and computational capability through dynamic network topology and quantum state adjustments. The core concept is to leverage quantum state self-maintenance, enabling the network to automatically adapt its structure and quantum state to counteract decoherence and maintain coherence. This paper details the design and implementation of QS-AN, exploring its mechanisms for stability, computational throughput, and scalability, aiming to address limitations inherent in traditional quantum network architectures. The system incorporates a dynamic network topology that responds to quantum state fluctuations, leading to a self-sustaining and adaptive quantum state. This research presents a significant advancement in quantum information processing, offering a potential pathway towards robust and scalable quantum computing.

title: Title: Temporal Resonance in Data Compression and Representation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of temporal resonance, a principle suggesting data patterns repeat at different scales, to revolutionize data compression and representation. Traditional compression methods often focus on statistical redundancy, while this work proposes an algorithm that leverages this inherent structure to achieve significantly higher compression ratios. We detail the core mechanism of identifying and compressing only the most significant elements based on temporal resonance, presenting a novel approach to data compression that moves beyond simple statistical analysis. The goal is to demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique through theoretical analysis and, to a limited extent, preliminary experimental testing. The core claim is that this temporal resonance-based compression algorithm can achieve compression ratios exceeding existing methods, offering a potentially transformative advancement in data storage and transmission.

title: Quantum Neural Networks with Dynamic Topological Structures
abstract: This paper presents a novel architecture for quantum neural networks (QNNs) characterized by dynamically adjustable topological structures. Traditional QNNs often suffer from limitations in scalability and adaptability, hindering their potential for complex computations. The proposed framework leverages quantum entanglement and interference to enable real-time modifications to the network's connectivity and topology. This dynamic capability is hypothesized to significantly enhance the learning efficiency and generalization performance of QNNs. title: # Black Gibbon: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Black Gibbon Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Black Gibbon, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the unique foraging behavior of black gibbons. Black gibbons exhibit a remarkable ability to rapidly and efficiently explore their environment, utilizing complex strategies to locate food sources. This paper details the design and implementation of Black Gibbon, focusing on its core mechanisms – the 'Shadowing' and 'Echoing' strategies – which mimic the gibbon's adaptive movements and information sharing. We demonstrate Black Gibbon's performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results indicate that Black Gibbon exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm's design incorporates a novel dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism based on the gibbon's observed foraging patterns, contributing to its robustness and adaptability. Future research directions include exploring the application of Black Gibbon to real-world engineering and scientific problems and further refining its core mechanisms through theoretical analysis.

title: Dynamic Semantic Reshaping Network (DSMNet)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Reshaping Network (DSMNet), a novel approach to adaptive computation that leverages reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust the semantic representation of computational nodes within a graph-structured network. The core claim of DSMNet is to achieve ultra-efficient adaptation by continuously reshaping the semantic representations of nodes and their connections, responding to evolving input data and task requirements. The proposed mechanism utilizes a Transformer-based reinforcement learning agent to optimize node semantic vectors, including their dimensionality, activation functions, and connection weights, based on observed outputs and task goals. Furthermore, the network dynamically adjusts connection weights to maximize signal transmission efficiency. DSMNet's architecture and control strategy represent a significant departure from traditional adaptive computation methods, offering a more nuanced and adaptable solution for complex, dynamic environments. The key innovation lies in the integration of semantic representation learning with reinforcement learning, enabling a truly adaptive system that can understand and respond to the inherent variability within data. ---

title: Dynamic Bayesian Networks for Explainable AI in Time Series
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to explainable artificial intelligence (AI) for time series data using Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs). Traditional Bayesian Networks often struggle to capture the complex temporal dependencies inherent in time series, leading to limited interpretability and predictive accuracy. Our proposed method addresses this limitation by constructing a DBN where node states evolve over time. Crucially, the network's structure itself adapts dynamically, guided by a time-varying Markov chain. This adaptation allows the DBN to learn and represent how temporal patterns influence relationships between variables, offering a significantly more nuanced and interpretable model compared to static Bayesian Networks. The core mechanism utilizes a time-varying Markov chain to govern the evolution of the network structure, enabling the representation of evolving dependencies. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline the key components required for implementation, highlighting its benefits for generating explanations within time series analysis. The system provides a richer understanding of the underlying processes driving the observed temporal patterns.
