title: Robust nonadiabatic holonomic gating in qutrits via inverse-engineered pulse shaping and error compensation
abstract: Systematic Rabi-amplitude and detuning errors remain important sources of infidelity in high-fidelity quantum gates. We develop a robust pulse-engineering scheme for non-adiabatic holonomic quantum computing in a three-level $Λ$-type qutrit, combining inverse engineering with time-dependent perturbative analysis. Pulse shaping eliminates the leading second-order Rabi-amplitude contribution, while static detuning introduces a distinct population-mediated channel that cannot be removed within a single control loop. We therefore introduce a compensation loop that exactly cancels the dominant second-order $O_{13}^δ$ contribution, with the residual $O_{12}^δ$ channel further suppressed by pulse shaping. Using the logical average gate fidelity over the complete computational subspace, the optimized composite sequence reaches closed-system fidelities of $99.88\%$--$99.99\%$ for four representative single-qubit gates at $ε=0.2$ and $δ/2π=2$ MHz. With phenomenological decoherence at $T_1=T_2=30~μ{\rm s}$, the NOT and S gates retain fidelities of $99.72\%$ and $99.79\%$, respectively, with a coherence-time crossover near $0.58~μ{\rm s}$. These results identify the regime in which systematic-error suppression outweighs the decoherence cost of the additional control loop.

title: Ownership of Copyright in AIGC Text-to-Image Works—A Case Study of the “Spring Breeze Case”
abstract: With the in-depth application of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AIGC) technology in the field of image creation, disputes over the ownership of copyright in text-to-image generated works have become a cutting-edge issue in intellectual property rights. Combining China’s first copyright dispute case involving AIGC text-to-image works (the “Spring Breeze Case”) and the adjudication rules of similar cases, this paper explores the core legal principles and practical issues of copyright protection for AIGC text-to-image works from four dimensions: the determination of work attributes, the analysis of copyright ownership subjects, the definition of infringement acts, and the construction of protection paths. The determination of copyright ownership for AIGC text-to-image works should return to the statutory core elements of originality and intellectual achievement. Natural person users, as technical practitioners, should be identified as copyright holders on the premise that the constituent elements of a work are satisfied. Meanwhile, a full-chain protection system for the copyright of AIGC text-to-image works should be constructed through multiple paths including legislative improvement, strengthened supervision, judicial unification, and enhanced burden of proof capacity of right holders.

title: Research Trends in K-12 Robot-Based Education in Korea for the Physical AI Era: Focusing on the Last Five Years
abstract: 피지컬 AI(Physical AI)의 부상으로 AI가 물리적 세계에서 자율적으로 인지·판단·행동하는 시대가 열리면서, 로봇을 활용한 SW·AI 교육의 중요성이 더욱 부각되고 있다. 본 연구는 피지컬 AI 시대를 대비하는 기초 교육으로서 국내 초·중·고 로봇 활용 교육의 연구 동향을 파악하기 위하여, 2020년부터 2025년 6월까지 발행된 국내 학술논문 중 초·중·고 학습자를 대상으로 한 92편을 분석하였다. 분석은 연구 시기, 연구 대상, 연구 유형, 사용된 로봇, 사용된 프로그래밍 언어, 로봇 활용 교육의 효과, 로봇 활용 SW·AI 교육의 7개 항목을 기준으로 진행하였다. 연구 결과, 최근 5년간 논문 수는 감소하였다가 증가하는 추세를 보였으며, 초등학생을 대상으로 한 연구와 설계 연구가 가장 많았다. 또한 레고 기반 로봇과 엔트리를 사용한 연구, 인지적 변인 중심의 연구가 다수를 차지하였다. 특히 로봇 활용 SW·AI 교육 관련 논문이 47편으로 전체의 과반을 차지하여, 로봇 교육이 AI 교육과 밀접히 연계되고 있음을 확인하였다. 본 연구는 피지컬 AI 시대의 맥락에서 국내 초·중·고 로봇 활용 교육 연구 동향을 체계적으로 분석하고, 향후 로봇 활용 교육 연구 및 실천에 대한 시사점을 제공한다는 점에서 의의를 지닌다.

title: SCILLA: Altitude-Coupled Transient Maritime Surface Observation — Geometry, Paired State Estimation, and Falsification of Adaptive Scan Allocation
abstract: SCILLA is an audited technical research programme investigating transient maritime surface observation using predominantly vertical platform motion as part of the sensing geometry. The work formalizes altitude-coupled surface-intercept geometry, ascent/return paired state estimation, resource-constrained scan allocation, an independent trace verifier, and a prepublication robustness programme. The central result is deliberately bounded. Adaptive scheduling does not universally improve raw discovery: in the frozen uniform synthetic reference regime, adaptive allocation underperforms the raster baseline on that endpoint. What survives is more specific. Across the declared synthetic reference regimes, adaptive allocation increases paired ascent/return observations and reduces the programme’s constructed priority-weighted Track Debt metric. The release includes the canonical technical research note, publication audit, robustness addendum, public claims register, reproducible protocol, run-level synthetic evidence, sensitivity and ablation analyses, source code, independent verifier, and standalone SCILLA simulation software. All quantitative performance results in this release are synthetic or model-derived unless explicitly identified otherwise. No physical SCILLA field-performance, 150 km detection capability, operational ROI, patent status, QPU execution, or quantum advantage is claimed. The next validation gates are external historical sensor replay and a cooperative paired-observation flight using synchronized platform navigation and independent target ground truth. SCILLA v1.1.0Michele Giletto — Giletto Systems Lab | Aerospace & Industrial Decision Research

title: Quantum Topologies: A Geometric Time Modeling Approach
abstract: Quantum Topologies offers a novel approach to time modeling, leveraging the inherent geometric properties of quantum states to predict the temporal evolution of quantum systems. This paper proposes a method based on the dynamic evolution of quantum states, driven by geometric principles, to achieve more precise quantum computation. We introduce a framework where the geometry of a quantum system governs its time behavior, offering a pathway to a deeper understanding of quantum dynamics. This work addresses the limitations of traditional time modeling by focusing on the geometric implications inherent in quantum mechanics. The core mechanism involves the evolution of quantum states through geometric transformations, yielding a predictive tool for temporal behavior. This approach promises to significantly enhance the accuracy and efficiency of quantum calculations.

title: Nonlinear Topological Geometry Quantum Entanglement Calculation Framework
abstract: This paper presents a novel computational framework for analyzing complex topological structures, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. We introduce a quantum entanglement state calculation model rooted in topological geometry, aiming to overcome the limitations of classical quantum computation in simulating intricate topological phenomena. The core mechanism involves incorporating a dynamic, non-linear structure within the quantum state, enabling a more precise and efficient representation of topological properties compared to traditional approaches. This framework offers a potential breakthrough in the simulation and analysis of complex topological geometries, particularly in scenarios where traditional methods struggle due to inherent complexity.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation Framework: Adaptive Geometry
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for transformative computational capabilities. This paper explores the design of a novel quantum computation framework, "Adaptive Geometry," centered around the manipulation of entangled states. This framework aims to dynamically adjust entanglement parameters, effectively enhancing quantum computation through a self-adaptive approach. The core mechanism involves leveraging the strength and path of entanglement to modulate its properties, fostering a more versatile and powerful computational landscape. We present a conceptual design and preliminary analysis of this framework, highlighting its potential to broaden the scope of quantum computation beyond existing algorithmic approaches.

title: 基于量子机器学习的非线性强化学习的自适应算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to reinforcement learning, leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum machine learning to develop an adaptive learning algorithm. Traditional reinforcement learning algorithms often struggle with complex environments due to the computational limitations of classical systems. We propose a quantum-enhanced learning framework that dynamically adjusts the learning strategy based on environmental changes, resulting in enhanced adaptation and exploration. This paper explores the potential of quantum mechanics to accelerate learning and improve the ability to navigate challenging environments. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to represent and update the state space more efficiently, facilitating faster convergence and the discovery of optimal policies. The proposed algorithm demonstrates promising results across a range of scenarios, showcasing its potential to overcome the limitations of classical reinforcement learning.

title: 混沌域的非线性几何映射与优化
abstract: This paper explores the application of a novel approach to optimization, leveraging the principles of chaos theory and non-linear geometry. We propose a framework that utilizes a dynamically evolving geometric map generated from the chaotic behavior of a defined region. This map allows the optimization algorithm to adapt to complex non-linear problems, potentially achieving superior performance compared to traditional gradient-based methods. The core mechanism centers on modeling the system's evolution through chaotic dynamics, enabling the algorithm to explore a broader search space and identify more robust global optima. This work introduces a new method for tackling optimization challenges by embracing the inherent unpredictability of chaotic systems.

title: Dynamic Quantum Error Correction Coding Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to dynamic quantum error correction (QEC) optimization, shifting the focus from solely relying on the structure of error-correcting codes to actively harnessing quantum entanglement generated during the coding process. The core claim is that the inherent entanglement between code-syndrome qubits can be leveraged to achieve dynamic performance improvements. The proposed mechanism involves real-time monitoring of entanglement strength between code-syndrome qubits and utilizing quantum operations to enhance specific entanglement links, thereby boosting error correction efficiency. This approach represents a fundamental departure from traditional static QEC design, offering the potential for adaptive and optimized error correction in quantum computing scenarios. Mathematical formulations and theoretical analysis are presented to support this dynamic entanglement-based optimization strategy. The key parameters influencing the optimization process are identified and quantified. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential challenges and future research directions.

title: Title: Constraint-Driven Emergent Algorithm Synthesis (CAESA)
abstract: This paper presents Constraint-Driven Emergent Algorithm Synthesis (CAESA), a novel algorithm designed to automatically generate new algorithms from a set of constraint sets. CAESA leverages an iterative process of constraint creation and algorithm generation, aiming to improve the efficiency of algorithm development through the discovery of novel solutions. The core mechanism focuses on creating constraints dynamically based on existing constraints, leading to an emergent algorithm synthesis process. The algorithm's design incorporates concepts of reinforcement learning and evolutionary algorithms to optimize the generation of complex and diverse algorithms. This work contributes to the field of automated algorithm design, offering a promising approach to tackling the challenges associated with algorithm creation and optimization.

title: Quantum-Inspired Constraint Satisfaction via Superconducting Qubits
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to solving constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) by leveraging principles inspired by quantum computing, specifically utilizing superconducting qubits. The core idea is to map the CSP's variables and constraints onto the state space of these qubits, then simulate a quantum annealing process through controlled decoherence and interference. Unlike traditional CSP solvers, this method aims to exploit the potential for rapid convergence by mimicking the superposition and entanglement characteristics inherent in quantum systems. The implementation described here is entirely classical, avoiding the need for specialized quantum hardware. We demonstrate a framework for translating CSP problems into a qubit-based representation and outlining the algorithmic steps for a 'quantum-inspired' annealing process. This approach offers a potentially scalable solution for complex CSPs, bridging the gap between classical computation and the theoretical advantages of quantum computation. The presented method focuses on achieving efficient exploration of the solution space through carefully designed control of qubit decoherence and interference, ultimately leading to near-optimal solutions. The key contribution lies in the practical realization of quantum-inspired algorithms using accessible, controllable superconducting qubits.

title: Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithms for Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: Hyperparameter optimization is a crucial step in the development and deployment of machine learning models. Traditional methods, like grid search and random search, often suffer from computational inefficiency, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional hyperparameter spaces. This paper explores the application of quantum-inspired techniques to accelerate hyperparameter optimization within evolutionary algorithms. We propose a framework where hyperparameter values are represented as quantum states, leveraging concepts like superposition and entanglement to explore the search space more efficiently. Specifically, we investigate the integration of quantum annealing-inspired operators and quantum walk-inspired strategies into the evolutionary algorithm framework. Our initial simulations demonstrate the potential for significant convergence speed improvements compared to standard evolutionary algorithms, suggesting that quantum-inspired approaches can offer a viable path towards faster and more effective hyperparameter tuning. We evaluate our approach using a standard dataset and a well-known machine learning model, showcasing the feasibility and potential advantages of this novel methodology. The core claim is that quantum-inspired techniques can accelerate the convergence of evolutionary algorithms. The core mechanism involves representing hyperparameter values as quantum states and employing quantum-inspired operators.

title: Quantum Information Space Structure Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the structure of quantum information spaces, exploring the inherent properties of information storage and propagation within these spaces. Utilizing advanced structure analysis techniques, we aim to uncover key characteristics and potential applications of quantum information within this framework. The core focus is on establishing a robust methodology for characterizing and manipulating quantum systems, with implications for both quantum algorithm design and secure quantum communication protocols. The research introduces a novel framework for analyzing and understanding the dynamic interplay of quantum states and their relationships, paving the way for enhanced performance and security in quantum technologies.

title: 拓扑场论的量子化
abstract: This paper explores the convergence of topological field quantization towards quantum computation, offering a novel approach to enhancing computational performance. We propose a method that leverages the inherent topological properties of fields to generate and manipulate quantum states, effectively circumventing certain limitations inherent in traditional quantum computing approaches. This work investigates the fundamental principles behind this strategy, detailing the mechanisms involved in transforming classical quantum states into a more manageable and controllable topological structure. The core claim is that this quantumization technique will yield significant improvements in computational capabilities, potentially paving the way for a new generation of quantum algorithms.

title: Bayesian Geometric Random Field (BGRF) Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces the Bayesian Geometric Random Field (BGRF) framework, a novel approach to analyzing and predicting the evolution of complex geometric random fields. The BGRF utilizes a Bayesian approach to model probabilistic evolution driven by latent variables and feedback loops, offering a unified framework for real-time adaptation and prediction. We demonstrate the BGRF's efficacy through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to capture intricate dynamics and provide insightful predictions compared to existing methods. The core mechanism lies in a probabilistic integration of geometric properties with dynamic evolution, enabling adaptive modeling and forecasting within a dynamically changing environment. This work represents a significant step towards a more robust and flexible tool for understanding and manipulating complex geometric systems.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Complexity - Pattern Recognition in Quantum Systems
abstract: Quantum-enhanced complexity represents a paradigm shift in pattern recognition, moving beyond classical algorithms to harness the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This research investigates a novel algorithm, Quantum-Enhanced Complexity (QEC), designed to detect subtle, non-classical correlations within complex datasets utilizing entanglement and superposition. We propose a framework that leverages these quantum phenomena to create a 'quantum fingerprint' for data, offering the potential for significantly enhanced pattern recognition capabilities. This paper details the core mechanism, explores potential applications, and outlines the challenges associated with implementing this approach. The study focuses on the specific benefits of entanglement-based pattern detection, arguing that it offers a distinct advantage in identifying subtle correlations often missed by traditional methods.

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Constraint Optimization
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Constraint Optimization (QICO) represents a novel approach to constraint optimization, incorporating the principles of quantum mechanics—specifically entanglement and superposition—to generate solutions robust to noise and possess enhanced potential. This paper proposes a new framework for constraint optimization utilizing quantum-inspired algorithms, designed to effectively mitigate the impact of real-world system noise during the optimization process. We detail the methodology, demonstrating its potential to improve the performance and reliability of AI systems across a range of challenging optimization problems. The core mechanism centers on generating solutions through a process of quantum-inspired manipulation, leveraging superposition and entanglement to achieve a greater range of possibilities and a more resilient solution space. This research provides a promising path towards creating more robust and adaptable AI systems.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive Bayesian network (ABN) gradient boosting algorithm designed to enhance learning capabilities and mitigate overfitting. Traditional gradient boosting methods often struggle with complex non-linear relationships and can be susceptible to instability. Our algorithm incorporates a dynamically adjusted learning rate mechanism, allowing the model to adapt to the data distribution and effectively navigate complex landscapes. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through extensive experimentation and analysis, achieving superior performance on a variety of benchmark datasets. title: Hierarchical State Space Exploration with Bayesian Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to reinforcement learning focused on efficient exploration of large and complex state spaces. The core idea is to construct a hierarchical representation of the state space and integrate Bayesian inference for robust uncertainty quantification. The system decomposes the state space into multiple levels of abstraction, each governed by a Bayesian reinforcement learning agent. These agents learn optimal policies within their respective sub-spaces, and information flows upwards through the hierarchy, facilitating both exploration and exploitation. This approach addresses the scalability issues inherent in traditional reinforcement learning methods, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional state spaces. title: Based on Quantum Entanglement: Non-Local Data Compression
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to data compression leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. Traditional data compression methods rely on identifying and eliminating redundancy within data, often achieving limitations in compression ratios. We propose a system that utilizes entangled quantum states to represent data, achieving potentially higher compression rates and, crucially, lossless reconstruction. The core idea involves decomposing data into a set of entangled quantum subsystems. By exploiting the inherent correlations present within entangled states, we can effectively reduce redundancy without losing information. The paper details the mathematical framework underlying this approach, focusing on the key concepts of entanglement, quantum measurement, and the reconstruction process. We outline the theoretical advantages of this method compared to conventional techniques and discuss the challenges associated with its practical implementation. The primary goal is to demonstrate the potential of quantum entanglement for fundamentally transforming data compression, moving beyond the constraints of classical redundancy reduction. ---

abstract: Quantum machine learning represents a paradigm shift in computational capabilities, offering the potential to solve complex problems currently intractable for classical algorithms. title: Adaptive Neural Symbolic Systems with Dynamic Rule Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Adaptive Neural Symbolic System (ANSS) designed to overcome the limitations of traditional neural-symbolic systems in dynamic environments. The core challenge lies in their inability to effectively adapt to new situations and generate new symbolic rules. Our approach addresses this by integrating a neural network with a dynamic rule generation mechanism, leveraging reinforcement learning to optimize a symbolic logic metric. The system observes its environment, uses the neural network to generate and refine symbolic rules, and continuously adjusts the ruleset based on feedback. This creates a system capable of adaptive reasoning and problem-solving, moving beyond static rule sets. The system's architecture and methodology are presented, outlining the key components and their interactions. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework and discuss future research directions. The primary innovation lies in the iterative, data-driven refinement of symbolic rules, enabling the system to learn and adapt in ways that are currently unavailable in conventional neural-symbolic architectures.

title: Quantum-Inspired Symbolic Regression with Adaptive Entanglement
abstract: Symbolic regression aims to discover mathematical equations from data, a task crucial in scientific discovery and model building. However, traditional symbolic regression methods often falter when dealing with high-dimensional, noisy datasets, plagued by the "curse of dimensionality" and the difficulty in identifying underlying patterns. This paper introduces a novel approach, Quantum-Inspired Symbolic Regression with Adaptive Entanglement (QISREA), designed to overcome these limitations. QISREA draws inspiration from quantum computing principles, particularly adaptive entanglement, to efficiently explore the vast search space of possible symbolic expressions. The core idea involves dynamically adjusting entanglement levels among potential terms in the equation based on the estimated data uncertainty. Higher entanglement signifies greater computational focus on regions of the search space deemed more promising, effectively mitigating the curse of dimensionality. We present a detailed formulation of the algorithm, outlining the key components including the initial entanglement distribution, the adaptive entanglement update rule, and the equation evaluation process. The effectiveness of QISREA is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a conceptual discussion, highlighting its potential advantages over conventional symbolic regression techniques.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Error Correction with Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum information processing offers unparalleled computational power, but the inherent fragility of quantum systems necessitates robust error correction. Traditional error correction codes struggle to effectively handle complex error profiles, hindering the realization of practical quantum technologies. This paper proposes an adaptive quantum error correction scheme leveraging neural networks to dynamically adjust error correction operations based on the observed error characteristics of a quantum system. We detail a novel training methodology for a neural network trained to predict and mitigate errors, resulting in improved error mitigation compared to existing approaches. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop, refining the neural network's error correction strategy in real-time, optimizing for both error correction and system fidelity. The potential benefits of this approach include increased error correction rates, reduced computational overhead, and improved overall system robustness. This research explores the practical implications of this adaptive scheme through simulations and preliminary experimental validations.

title: ## Batak White-toothed Shrew: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Batak White-toothed Shrew" (BWTS), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Suncus murinus* (Batak white-toothed shrew). These shrews exhibit a unique and remarkably efficient foraging strategy characterized by a combination of exploratory and exploitative phases, punctuated by periods of inactivity. BWTS leverages these observed behaviors to develop an optimization algorithm designed for complex, multi-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm incorporates key elements such as a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, a memory-based adaptive learning mechanism mirroring the shrew's selective recall of favorable foraging locations, and a novel "nesting" strategy to manage the population size. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The core of BWTS is presented through a set of equations detailing its key parameters and operations. This research aims to contribute a new optimization technique rooted in biological inspiration, exhibiting robust performance and adaptability in challenging optimization problems.

title: Baptista Lake Titi: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of a Unique Fish Species
abstract: This paper presents Baptista Lake Titi (BLT), a newly developed metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the *Baptista lake titi* (also known as *Synbranchus marmoratus*), a unique fish species inhabiting freshwater lakes in South America. BLT leverages the fish's dynamic movement patterns, specifically its ability to rapidly adapt to changing environmental conditions and its preference for areas with high resource concentration, to create a robust and efficient optimization process. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive inertia weight mechanism, a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, and a unique 'pulse' mechanism mimicking the fish's sporadic bursts of movement. The performance of BLT is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive ability against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that BLT exhibits strong convergence properties and adaptability, making it a promising alternative for various complex optimization tasks. The core of the algorithm lies in simulating the fish's response to varying food availability and predator pressure, translating these behavioral traits into effective search strategies within the optimization landscape. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and experimental results, providing a comprehensive analysis of its capabilities and potential applications.

title: ## Argentine Fat-tailed Opossum: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed Argentine Fat-tailed Opossum (AFTO), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Argentine fat-tailed opossum (Didelphis earina). The algorithm leverages the opossum's unique strategy of exploring diverse food sources with a weighted probability distribution based on their perceived value. AFTO incorporates a novel adaptive weighting scheme, combined with a simulated annealing-like temperature control mechanism and a stochastic local search component, to effectively navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic methods like Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of probabilities based on a 'fat-tailed' distribution, reflecting the opossum's preference for less-explored, potentially higher-value solutions. We demonstrate AFTO's efficacy in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions for diverse optimization challenges. The algorithm's parameters are designed for robustness and adaptability, making it suitable for various application domains.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Chaotic Dynamics
abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) has demonstrated remarkable success in modeling nonlinear dynamics, yet its performance is often limited by the inherent representational capacity of traditional recurrent neural networks. This work proposes a novel approach, Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing (QIRC), which seeks to overcome these limitations by incorporating principles from quantum mechanics. Specifically, we introduce a "quantum reservoir" – a recurrent neural network where nodes exist in a superposition of states and connections are governed by probabilistic entanglement rules. title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding: A Theoretical Evolution
abstract: This paper investigates the theoretical foundations and practical implications of quantum entanglement information encoding. Traditional information encoding methods are limited by their reliance on classical physics. We propose a novel approach utilizing quantum entanglement to enhance information security and key distribution, offering a potential paradigm shift in data protection. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the unique properties of entangled particles to facilitate significantly more efficient information transfer and secure key distribution compared to existing techniques. This work explores the mathematical underpinnings of this framework, including the encoding and decoding protocols. The paper demonstrates the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and explores its strengths and weaknesses. The research highlights the challenges and future directions for further development, emphasizing the need for rigorous mathematical validation and experimental testing. We conclude by outlining the key mathematical contributions and the potential impact of this theory on the field of quantum information.

title: ## Antelope Jackrabbit Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Antelope Jackrabbit Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Antelope Jackrabbit Algorithm (AJA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Antelope Jackrabbits. These animals exhibit remarkable adaptability to environmental changes and efficient path planning strategies when searching for food sources. The AJA algorithm leverages these characteristics to develop a novel optimization technique. The core concept involves simulating the jackrabbit's movement pattern, incorporating elements of exploration and exploitation, and using a unique adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. The fitness function is evaluated based on the distance traveled and the food source found. The proposed AJA algorithm is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that the AJA algorithm possesses promising potential for complex optimization problems where adaptability and rapid response to environmental changes are crucial. Key parameters influencing the algorithm's performance are analyzed, and future research directions are discussed.

title: Adaptive Matrix Quantumization Calculation Dynamic Encryption
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum cryptography leveraging adaptive matrix quantization. Traditional cryptographic methods often rely on static key parameters, which can be vulnerable to various attacks. This work introduces a dynamic encryption strength adjustment mechanism, dynamically adjusting the quantum state based on matrix modifications, thereby enhancing security and algorithmic stability. We detail the design of the adaptive matrix quantization process, its mathematical foundation, and its potential benefits for secure communication. The core claim focuses on the ability to dynamically adjust encryption strength to combat evolving threats, offering a more robust security posture.

title: Angolan Epauletted Fruit Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Epauletted Fruit Bat Optimization" (EFBO), inspired by the foraging behavior of Angolan Epauletted Fruit Bats ( *Pteropus angolensis*). These bats exhibit a unique and highly efficient foraging strategy characterized by a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance and a strong preference for areas with high food concentration. The EFBO algorithm leverages these characteristics to develop a robust optimization approach. The core of the algorithm incorporates a novel movement mechanism based on the bats' flight patterns, incorporating a distance-based exploration component and a food-concentration-based exploitation component. The algorithm's parameters are designed to mimic the bats' behavior, specifically the 'epaulet' movement and the 'food-seeking' tendencies. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations and theoretical analysis, showcasing its performance across a range of benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that EFBO exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA), particularly in problems with complex landscapes and multimodal solutions. Future work will focus on adaptive parameter tuning and the integration of the algorithm into real-world applications.

title: Title: Geometric Regularization for Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric regularization to adaptive neural networks, aiming to enhance their generalization capabilities through the introduction of a novel loss function that explicitly penalizes deviations from a predefined geometric constraint. The core mechanism involves modifying the training objective to incentivize representations that are more robust and adaptable, offering a potential pathway to improved model performance across diverse datasets. We present a framework that dynamically adjusts the regularization strength based on the network's internal representation, promoting a more nuanced and effective regularization strategy. This work contributes to the growing field of adaptive learning, specifically focusing on enhancing the robustness of neural networks through geometric principles.

title: ## River Perch Spotting Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Method Inspired by River Perch Melanism
abstract: River perch ( *Péryllo corbiculatus* ) exhibits a fascinating phenomenon known as melanism, characterized by irregular brown spots distributed across its body. This unique pattern has inspired the development of a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the River Perch Spotting Algorithm (RPSA). RPSA mimics the dynamic adaptation and localized changes observed in the melanistic pattern of river perch, specifically focusing on the competition and dispersal of pigment cells. The algorithm employs a population-based approach where individuals represent potential solutions. Each individual's 'spot' distribution is governed by a stochastic process influenced by a 'spot density' and 'spot movement' factor. The algorithm utilizes a novel 'spot merging' and 'spot splitting' mechanism to promote diversity and exploration, and a 'spot competition' strategy to guide exploitation. The core principle is to simulate the dynamic interaction between pigment cells, reflecting the adaptive nature of melanism. This paper details the theoretical framework, the algorithm's components, and its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: Quantum Error Correction Underpins Distributed Machine Learning Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum error correction (QEC) codes to enhance distributed machine learning (DML) optimization. The core claim is that QEC's inherent noise mitigation capabilities can significantly improve the robustness and efficiency of DML model training. The proposed mechanism involves encoding machine learning model parameters into quantum states, utilizing QEC for inter-node communication and computation, and concurrently performing error detection and correction. This represents a novel approach, as QEC and DML have historically been pursued independently. The research investigates the theoretical underpinnings of this integration, focusing on key aspects such as code selection, communication protocols, and error correction strategies within the distributed environment. We examine the impact of varying noise levels and communication constraints on the overall performance of the DML system. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate a framework where QEC's capabilities can be directly translated into a more reliable and scalable DML solution.

title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Strategies and Genetic Programming
abstract: Symbolic regression is a technique that aims to discover mathematical equations from data. Despite its potential, traditional methods often face challenges when dealing with high-dimensional data and intricate relationships. This paper introduces a novel approach combining evolutionary strategies (ES) and genetic programming (GP) to address these limitations. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both techniques: GP for generating potentially accurate expression structures, and ES for fine-tuning the parameters within those structures. We propose a hybrid system where GP iteratively constructs symbolic expressions, and ES simultaneously optimizes the parameters associated with those expressions. This integrated strategy significantly enhances the exploration of the search space, leading to improved accuracy and, importantly, a greater tendency towards simpler, more interpretable models. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to standalone GP and ES approaches. We define the following key notations: *x* - input vector, *f(x)* - function output, *S* - set of mathematical operators (e.g., +, -, *, /), *p* - parameter vector, *E* - symbolic expression, *|E|* - length of the expression, *||E||_1 - L1 norm of the expression, *||E||_2 - L2 norm of the expression*. The system is designed to minimize the error between the predicted function value and the actual data points while simultaneously promoting simplicity.

title: Alfaro's Rice Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Sigmodon hispidus*
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Alfaro's Rice Rat" (ARR), inspired by the foraging strategies of *Sigmodon hispidus*, commonly known as the rice rat. Rice rats are renowned for their efficient and adaptive foraging behavior, particularly their ability to exploit patchy environments and dynamically adjust their search patterns based on resource availability and perceived risk. The ARR algorithm leverages these observed characteristics to develop a new metaheuristic approach for solving complex optimization problems. The core of the algorithm centers on a simulated "patch exploration" mechanism, where solutions are represented as "foraging territories," and a dynamic "risk assessment" module guides the search process. The algorithm incorporates a novel "memory" component inspired by the rice rat's cognitive mapping of food sources, allowing for efficient revisiting of promising regions. We outline the algorithm's theoretical foundations, its key components, and present a conceptual overview of its operation. Performance analysis is discussed through a series of examples, demonstrating the algorithm's potential in tackling challenging optimization problems. The algorithm is presented as a flexible framework adaptable to various problem domains.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Imbalanced Dataset Through Data Augmentation and Generative Annotation Using DistilBERT and Low‐Rank Fine‐Tuning
abstract: ABSTRACT Sentiment analysis on social media data often suffers from severe class imbalance, which can negatively affect the performance of machine learning models. In this paper, we propose a framework that leverages large language models and lightweight transformer fine tuning to improve sentiment classification on imbalanced datasets. First, GPT‐4, a multimodal large language model, is used to generate synthetic tweets through paraphrasing and back translation, with Italian serving as an intermediate language, to increase data diversity. In addition, GPT‐4 is employed to annotate tweets with positive reasons by generating semantic counterparts to the 10 predefined negative categories in the Twitter US Airline Sentiment dataset. This process enables the creation of meaningful positive annotations derived from existing category structures, thereby improving dataset balance and interpretability. The augmented data are then encoded using DistilBERT to obtain sentence embeddings, while low rank adaptation (LoRA) is applied for efficient fine tuning with reduced computational cost. Finally, a SoftMax classifier is used to predict sentiment labels (positive, neutral, and negative). Experimental results on the Twitter US Airline Sentiment dataset—evaluated rigorously using a held‐out test set and 10‐fold cross‐validation—demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves strong classification performance while maintaining low training complexity, highlighting the effectiveness of combining Large Language Model (LLM) based data augmentation with parameter‐efficient transformer adaptation.

title: WiSDoM: Wireless Sparse Decision Transformer with Mixture-of-Experts for Multi-Task Mobile Network Optimization
abstract: Emerging 6G wireless networks are expected to operate across diverse deployment scenarios, where variations in network topology, user mobility, traffic demand, and radio conditions challenge the scalability of conventional radio resource management (RRM). While offline reinforcement learning (RL) methods have demonstrated strong decision-making capabilities, learning a single policy that performs consistently across heterogeneous wireless environments remains difficult due to conflicting optimization objectives and limited model specialization. These challenges become particularly pronounced in coordinated multipoint (CoMP) transmission, where selecting the optimal serving-cell combination requires sequential decision-making under evolving network conditions. This paper presents the Wireless Sparse Decision Transformer with Mixture of Experts (WiSDoM), a sparse multi-task offline RL framework for adaptive multi-cell selection. WiSDoM combines Decision Transformers (DTs) with a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture that dynamically activates specialized experts according to task characteristics. This MoE mechanism improves model capacity without proportionally increasing inference cost, mitigates negative transfer, and enables expert specialization across tasks. WiSDoM is trained jointly on diverse network configurations spanning multiple base station and user equipment densities, mobility levels, and scheduler policies. Experimental results show that WiSDoM consistently outperforms heuristic methods, single-task models, and conventional multi-task DTs, improving quality of experience (QoE) by up to 55% while activating approximately one-third of the parameters of its dense counterpart during inference. Furthermore, WiSDoM exhibits strong task generalization and efficiently adapts to unseen wireless scenarios through few-shot prompting without retraining or fine-tuning.

title: Quantum Secret Sharing with a Helper and Programmable Access Structures
abstract: Quantum secret sharing (QSS) is a process in which the state of a quantum system is partitioned into multiple shares, allowing only specific subsets of shareholders to reconstruct the state, while others gain no information about its identity. In this work, we propose a variant of QSS, called ``helper QSS,'' which designates a special shareholder whose participation with any other group of parties is sufficient for recovering the state. We present different families of helper codes that function for an arbitrary number of parties and system sizes. As an application, we introduce the idea of a programmable access structure in QSS, which allows for a third-party programmer to independently choose the access structure of the code even after the shares are delivered to all the shareholders. This choice is made blindly, meaning that the programmer has no information about the secret being encoded, and it is implemented using the nonlocal process of quantum steering.

title: Bosonic codes from compact phase spaces
abstract: We present the algebraic structure of bosonic quantum error-correcting codes on genus-two Riemann surfaces. We explicitly construct the code words as automorphic forms and analytically generate the full tower of code spaces at all weights. We prove a fundamental no-go theorem: for any genus greater than one, the stabilizer group is non-amenable, forcing a strictly positive spectral gap in the stabilizer Hamiltonian. Consequently, no normalizable quantum state can satisfy all stabilizer conditions. This sharply contrasts with standard Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes, where the amenability of the stabilizer group $\mathbb{Z}^2$ permits approximate code words with arbitrary precision.

title: Geometric Attractor Monitoring: A Robust and Frugal Framework for Multi-modal Industrial Robotic Cycles
abstract: Monitoring the health of heterogeneous industrial robot fleets is severely challenged by the multi-modal nature of their operational cycles and a persistent scarcity of run-to-failure data. Standard data-driven approaches, particularly deep learning architectures relying on sequential reconstruction, often struggle in this specific setting; they tend to over-smooth complex dynamics, masking early signs of degradation. To address these industrial constraints, we reframe the monitoring problem through a framework based on Phase Space Reconstruction (PSR). Instead of predicting temporal sequences, this framework transforms univariate sensor data into a geometric attractor, explicitly unfolding the mechanical states independently of their temporal occurrence. By evaluating various anomaly scoring techniques within this space, we demonstrate that discrete support estimation provides an effective and computationally frugal Health Indicator (HI). Validated on a real-world dataset of 21 heterogeneous robots over three years and a synthetic Langevin system, our approach outperforms standard deep learning baselines. We show that aligning the algorithmic bias with the geometric properties of the target system yields a pragmatic, traceable and easily deployable approach perfectly tailored to the realities of industrial constraints.

title: Collapsibility of Performance Metrics in Clinical Predictive AI
abstract: Background: Population level assessments of predictive artificial intelligence (AI) can conceal performance disparities across subgroups. Fairness evaluations commonly rely on performance analyses across subgroups. However, some performance metrics are non-collapsible, meaning that the overall population performance value does not equal the weighted average of subgroup specific values. Objective: To examine the collapsibility properties of commonly reported performance metrics in predictive AI, with a focus on the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC, also known as c-statistic). Methods: We investigate the collapsibility of 15 performance metrics, either by expressing each metric as a linear combination of its stratum specific values or, where non-collapsible, by providing a counterexample inspired by Simpson's paradox as a formal disproof. Results: Five performance metrics (AUC, calibration intercept, calibration slope, expected calibration error, and Nagelkerke R^2) are shown to be non-collapsible, and ten (O:E ratio, logloss, Brier score, accuracy, F1-score, true positive rate, true negative rate, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and net benefit) are shown to be collapsible. The AUC is shown to be non-collapsible because it decomposes into within- and cross-group AUC terms when subpopulations coexist, such that its overall value may fall outside the range of subgroup specific AUCs. Conclusions: Non-collapsibility of performance metrics has important consequences for reporting, model appraisal, and fairness evaluation. It can generate spurious differences between subgroup and overall performance, which may mislead fairness evaluations. Explicitly acknowledging and reporting the collapsibility properties of performance metrics improves both the interpretability and transparency of fairness assessments.

Results: Five performance metrics (AUC, calibration intercept, calibration slope, expected calibration error, and Nagelkerke R^2) are shown to be non-collapsible, and ten (O:E ratio, logloss, Brier score, accuracy, F1-score, true positive rate, true negative rate, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and net benefit) are shown to be collapsible. The AUC is shown to be non-collapsible because it decomposes into within- and cross-group AUC terms when subpopulations coexist, such that its overall value may fall outside the range of subgroup specific AUCs. Conclusions: Non-collapsibility of performance metrics has important consequences for reporting, model appraisal, and fairness evaluation. It can generate spurious differences between subgroup and overall performance, which may mislead fairness evaluations. Explicitly acknowledging and reporting the collapsibility properties of performance metrics improves both the interpretability and transparency of fairness assessments.

title: Beyond Churn: Predicting Financial Fragmentation in Retail Banking with Temporal Machine Learning
abstract: Retail banking attrition is usually represented as a terminal binary event, even though client relationships often weaken earlier through partial movements of deposits, investments, and recurring activity to external financial institutions. This paper defines that preceding state as financial fragmentation and presents an end-to-end temporal machine-learning system for predicting it before complete disengagement. Using anonymized multi-source data from a large retail bank, the framework predicts whether a valid external transfer or investment event will occur within 90 days. The study uses 595,220 client-month observations, with 346 engineered features combining monthly client profiles, balances, product relationships, prior flow-of-funds behavior, macroeconomic conditions, and competitor activity. A four-stage XGBoost cascade estimates (1) whether an external outflow will occur within 90 days, (2) the expected amount, (3) the originating product, and (4) the destination financial institution. The primary classifier achieved a test precision-recall area under the curve of 0.823. At the validation-selected threshold, it produced 86.4% precision, 75.1% recall, and an F1 score of 0.803. Ranking test observations in descending Stage 1 fragmentation score, the top 1% of clients yielded 95.3% precision, while the top 5% captured 78.7% of observed outflow cases. The amount model placed 94.9% of predictions within an adjacent amount bucket. Destination prediction reached a macro-F1 of 0.81 across 27 classes; source-product prediction achieved a weighted F1 of 0.92. By moving the analytical focus from terminal churn to earlier fund migration, the proposed approach provides a practical foundation for proactive, explainable, and economically informed client-retention decision support.

title: CellPrior-net: Prior-guided nuclei detection and classification for H&E whole-slide images
abstract: Accurate nuclei detection and classification in hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) is a key task in computational pathology, particularly for quantitative analysis of the tumor microenvironment. However, this task remains highly challenging due to variations in nuclei morphology, staining procedures, scanners, organs, magnifications, and WSI artifacts. In addition, many existing pipelines rely on computationally demanding architectures and post-processing procedures, making gigapixel WSI analysis time-consuming. In this work, CellPrior-Net (CP-Net) is proposed, an efficient nuclei detection and classification pipeline that utilizes a lightweight convolutional neural network architecture and hematoxylin (H) channel as prior information to enhance nuclei-aware feature learning. Extensive benchmarking was conducted against state-of-the-art pipelines on eight public and private datasets (total:∼10.4 M nuclei) obtained from different organs, scanners, magnifications, and clinical centers. Experimental results demonstrate that CP-Net achieves comparable performance while significantly reducing inference time. Furthermore, CellQuant-Net was introduced-an end-to-end nuclei quantification pipeline-that integrates a quality assessment model to exclude regions with artifacts, followed by CP-Net cell detection and classification. The pipeline is publicly available on GitHub, and provides a potentially efficient and scalable framework for downstream computational pathology applications.

title: A Performance Evaluation Of Feature-Based And Generative Anomaly Detection Paradigms Under CPU Resource Constraints
abstract: Unsupervised visual anomaly detection in industrial and clinical edge environments faces a critical dual challenge: the absolute scarcity of anomalous training samples and the prohibitive deployment costs of high-power GPU infrastructures. To bridge this gap, this paper presents a comprehensive evaluation and deployment framework that cross-analyzes two major deep learning paradigms—generative reconstructive models (Autoencoder, VAE, GANomaly, and Deep SVDD) and non-parametric feature-based descriptors (PaDiM, Patch-Based, and PatchCore)—optimized exclusively for resource-constrained CPU environments. Rather than relying on expensive hardware scaling, our methodology leverages transfer learning via a frozen ResNet34 backbone, combined with geometric Coreset compression and high-performance vector indexing through the FAISS CPU library. Extensive cross-evaluation on the MVTec AD, Industrial Rock, and Chest X-Ray datasets reveals a stark architectural polarization. While generative architectures struggle with semantic representations—manifesting a severe performance degradation on complex clinical textures with a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) AUROC dropping to 0.3301 due to the Blurry Reconstruction Syndrome—the optimized non-parametric feature models achieve a near-perfect AUROC of 0.9991. Crucially, through rigorous software engineering, our unified ecosystem reduces inference latency to an ultra-fast sub-millisecond threshold (< 0.8 ms per frame) on conventional, low-power desktop hardware. Finally, this work formalizes the theoretical boundaries of these paradigms by contrasting the Blurry Reconstruction Syndrome against the metrological paradox of the Gray Zone, where global scalar anomaly score reductions produce marginal false negatives despite flawless spatial pixel-level localization via heatmaps. This benchmark establishes a new blueprint for eco-efficient, highly sustainable One-Class AI deployment at the industrial edge.

title: Dynamic Topic Modeling (DTM) based on Pre-trained Language Model (SBERT) for Defense Technology Patent Big Data Analysis: Focusing on Weapon Systems Before and After the Ukraine War
abstract: 국방 R&D 환경의 불확실성이 급증함에 따라 기술 문헌으로부터 유의미한 동향을 추출하는 텍스트 마이닝의 중요성이 대두되고 있다. 기존 기술 예측 연구에서 주로 활용된 잠재 디리클레 할당 모델(LDA)은 전문 용어가 혼재되고 문맥적 의미가 복잡한 국방 분야의 비정형 텍스트를 군집화하는 데 구조적 한계를 지닌다. 본 연구는 이러한 한계를 극복하기 위해 트랜스포머 아키텍처 기반의 사전학습 언어모델(SBERT)과 밀도 기반 군집화(HDBSCAN)를 결합한 BERTopic 알고리즘의 국방 도메인 적용 타당성을 검증하였다. 2018년부터 2025년까지 출원된 12,773건의 글로벌 무기체계 특허 데이터를 대상으로 정량적 성능 평가를 수행한 결과, 전통적 플랫폼에서 지능형 비대칭 전력으로의 R&D 패러다임 전환 현상을 입증하였다.

title: Quantum State Random Generation and Topological Structure Association
abstract: This paper investigates the generation of quantum states through a novel random generation process, aiming to produce quantum states exhibiting complex topological structures. We propose a framework leveraging quantum state randomness to create new quantum states with intricate topological properties. The core mechanism involves iteratively modifying quantum states to induce topological defects, which are then utilized to generate higher-dimensional quantum states with enhanced topological features. The resulting system is designed to facilitate the exploration and manipulation of topological structures in quantum systems. This research presents a unique approach to quantum state creation, potentially offering a pathway towards advanced quantum technologies and a deeper understanding of topological quantum phenomena.

title: 基于拓扑几何的量子计算拓扑特征提取
abstract: Quantum computing is rapidly advancing, and the ability to accurately simulate quantum systems is crucial for realizing practical quantum algorithms. Traditional methods often struggle with the complexities inherent in quantum systems, particularly those exhibiting intricate topological features. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum state simulation based on topological geometry, utilizing the inherent structure of quantum states to achieve precise and efficient simulation. We introduce a method that leverages the geometry of quantum states to enhance the accuracy and speed of quantum calculations. This approach offers a significant improvement over existing techniques, particularly when dealing with systems exhibiting complex topological structures. The core mechanism involves a sophisticated mapping process that transforms quantum states into geometric representations, enabling precise modeling and optimization. This research explores the potential of this methodology to unlock new capabilities in quantum computing, focusing on the extraction of crucial topological features.

title: 自适应时空几何优化模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive spacetime geometry optimization model designed to address spatial separation and data fusion challenges. Traditional approaches often rely on static models, limiting their adaptability to dynamic environments. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts spacetime geometry based on input data and environmental changes, offering a more robust and flexible solution. The core mechanism involves the construction of a dynamic spacetime geometry transformation system, enabling automated optimization of spatial separation and data fusion. The model demonstrates significant improvements in these key areas through rigorous analysis and simulation.

title: Dynamic Matrices and Quantum Qubit Arithmetic
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic matrices and quantum qubit arithmetic to revolutionize matrix operations. The core focus is the development of a novel non-linear mapping for dynamic matrices, leveraging the power of quantum qubit arithmetic to achieve a form of quantum computation within the context of matrix operations. Mathematical rigor is employed throughout, providing a detailed analysis of the proposed mechanism and its implications for computational efficiency and potential algorithmic advancements. The paper concludes with a validation of the core concepts through rigorous mathematical proofs.

title: Dynamic Space Logic Adaptive Reasoning Engine
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic space logic reasoning engine designed to enhance inference efficiency and accuracy through adaptive reasoning path and parameter adjustments. The core concept is the "Dynamic Space" paradigm, where the reasoning process is modeled as a space of points, where the relationships between points are defined by dynamically adjusting rules. The engine achieves this adaptability by incorporating a self-tuning mechanism that continuously refines the inference process based on local data variations. We detail the implementation of this dynamic space concept, its associated algorithms, and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulated scenarios. This work represents a significant advancement in reasoning engine design, offering a robust and adaptable approach to tackling complex problems.

title: Geometry Language Automated Inference – A Formal Logic-Based Topology Verification
abstract: This paper explores the application of formal logic to automated inference of topology verification rules. Traditional methods for verifying topology transformations are often labor-intensive and lack scalability. We propose a novel system utilizing a formally defined language to establish a rigorous verification framework. This system leverages the power of formal logic to automatically generate and validate topology transformation rules, enhancing the reliability and precision of these transformations. The core mechanism centers on constructing a strict validation protocol using formal logic, ensuring the correctness of the transformation through rigorous mathematical analysis. The system aims to address the limitations of manual verification, offering a scalable and dependable approach to topology analysis.

title: Title: Adaptive Topological Group Constraint
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive topological constraint method for system optimization. Traditional optimization techniques often rely on explicit, static constraints, which may be insufficient for complex systems exhibiting dynamic behavior. This work proposes a novel approach that leverages the inherent topological structure of systems to establish adaptive constraints, guiding the system towards desired outcomes. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic topology based on system state and evolution, allowing for real-time adjustments and improved performance. This research offers a fundamentally different perspective on optimization, capitalizing on the unique properties of topological groups to achieve optimal solutions across a wide range of applications. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through simulations and analyses, showcasing significant improvements in performance compared to conventional optimization strategies.

title: Quantum Topological Field Theory
abstract: Quantum Topological Field Theory (QTF) presents a novel approach to quantum computation, leveraging the principles of quantum field theory and topological quantum mechanics. This paper explores the concept of a "topological field" – a fundamental building block – and its integration with quantum field theory to achieve unprecedented computational capabilities. We detail the core mechanism of constructing a quantum state representation based on quantum entanglement, aiming to fundamentally revolutionize the understanding of quantum entanglement. This research aims to address limitations of existing quantum computing paradigms by introducing a fundamentally new computational architecture predicated on topological properties.

title: Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for System Complexity Adaptive Control
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to system control utilizing multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) with adaptive complexity management. The core idea is to decompose a complex system into multiple sub-systems, each controlled by an individual agent trained using MARL. Crucially, a central system monitors the overall system complexity and dynamically adjusts the strategies of the individual agents to ensure stable and efficient operation. This adaptive control mechanism enhances robustness and adaptability, particularly in environments exhibiting high complexity and uncertainty. The proposed framework addresses limitations of traditional control methods by allowing for decentralized control and continuous adaptation to changing conditions. Mathematical formulations and key concepts are presented to provide a comprehensive understanding of the methodology. The system's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, demonstrating the potential for significant improvements in complex system control scenarios. ---

title: Non-Linear Quantum Circuit Optimization
abstract: Quantum circuit optimization is a crucial challenge in quantum computing, particularly for realizing complex quantum algorithms. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manually defined parameters, limiting their adaptability to varying circuit designs. This paper introduces a novel approach based on machine learning to dynamically adjust circuit structure during optimization, thereby enhancing circuit efficiency. We propose a self-adaptive optimization strategy that learns circuit characteristics and automatically refines the circuit's layout to achieve optimal performance. The core mechanism leverages a neural network to learn and predict optimal circuit parameter adjustments, allowing for a more flexible and efficient optimization process. This research offers a significant advancement in quantum circuit design, addressing a key limitation of existing techniques.

title: 基于多宇宙的机器学习
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning framework, termed "Multi-Universe Machine Learning" (MUML), which leverages the principles of multiple universes to enhance data augmentation and feature learning. Traditional machine learning models often struggle with complex data distributions due to their reliance on limited data. MUML utilizes a multi-universe probabilistic model to dynamically generate synthetic data from multiple universes, effectively expanding the training dataset and improving model robustness and adaptability. The core mechanism centers around the creation of multiple "universes" – simulated environments representing distinct data distributions – and the strategic extraction and integration of features across these universes. This approach allows for a more robust and adaptable model, particularly beneficial for complex datasets and tasks requiring high generalization capabilities. The paper explores the benefits of this framework through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments demonstrating improved performance on a benchmark dataset.

title: Title: Automated Proof of Concept for Higher-Order Logic
abstract: This paper presents a novel system for automated proof of concept generation and verification for complex higher-order logical statements. Recognizing the significant bottleneck in formal verification, we introduce a Constraint-Driven Inference Engine (CDIE) – an AI-powered system designed to rapidly generate and rigorously validate proofs of concept. The CDIE leverages deep learning to learn complex logical patterns and apply them to novel scenarios, dramatically reducing the time and effort traditionally required for this crucial stage of software development and formal reasoning. This work demonstrates the potential of such an approach to significantly advance the field, offering a transformative solution for complex logical analysis.

title: Quantum Topology Based Computation: A Novel Approach to Precision and Efficiency
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field of physics, offers a unique paradigm for manipulating and controlling quantum states. This paper explores the application of quantum topology to computation, focusing on a novel computational framework predicated on the principles of quantum self-adaptation. We propose a method that automatically adjusts the computation process's parameters, leading to significantly enhanced precision and efficiency compared to traditional algorithms. This approach addresses limitations of existing optimization strategies by enabling dynamic parameter tuning during computation. The core mechanism relies on the inherent properties of quantum systems to achieve precise results with minimal computational overhead. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its potential for advancing the state of quantum computing.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology: A Novel Approach to Adaptive Topological Quantum Systems
abstract: This paper explores the potential of dynamic quantum topology as a framework for generating and adapting complex topological quantum states. Traditional topological quantum systems often rely on static models, limiting their ability to accurately represent and predict behavior in dynamic environments. We propose a dynamic quantum topology algorithm that iteratively adjusts the underlying quantum structure to respond to environmental changes, offering a novel approach to simulating and predicting topological properties. The core mechanism involves a series of quantum operations designed to evolve the topology while simultaneously incorporating feedback loops based on measured environmental data. This paper details the design of the algorithm, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental explorations demonstrating its adaptability. We conclude with a discussion of the potential applications of this approach in various fields, including quantum information processing and materials science.

title: Beecroft's Anomalure: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Anomalure Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Beecroft's Anomalure, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Anomalures, small South American rodents known for their unique burrowing and caching strategies. The algorithm, termed 'Anomalure Search' (AS), leverages the Anomalure's adaptive response to environmental changes and resource scarcity to optimize solutions in complex search spaces. AS employs a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), incorporating a novel 'Cache Adaptation' mechanism that mimics the Anomalure's caching behavior to guide exploration and exploitation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of parameters based on the perceived 'resource density' within the search space, mirroring the Anomalure's ability to prioritize areas with higher potential rewards. This paper details the algorithm's design, provides mathematical formulations for key components, and presents experimental results highlighting its capabilities and potential applications. The primary objective is to demonstrate how biological inspiration, specifically the Anomalure's foraging strategy, can lead to a robust and effective metaheuristic algorithm.

title: Quantum State Prediction: Adaptive Geometric Transformations
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state prediction algorithm based on adaptive geometric transformations. The core claim is that this algorithm can automatically adjust the geometric transformations used in quantum state prediction, leading to improved accuracy, reduced latency, and the detection of subtle quantum state variations. This approach leverages the unique characteristics of high-dimensional geometric transformations to dynamically optimize the prediction process. We detail the algorithm's design, including the use of a predictive model and the implementation of geometric transformation adjustment. The resulting algorithm demonstrates enhanced precision and reduced latency compared to traditional methods, and highlights the detection of small quantum state changes. The study is motivated by the challenges of maintaining high fidelity in quantum communication protocols and the need for robust error mitigation techniques.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization Design Based on Quantum Genetic Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimization design leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and entanglement, through a Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA). Traditional Genetic Algorithms (GAs) face challenges in complex, high-dimensional optimization problems due to the exponential growth of the search space. The QGA aims to mitigate these limitations by encoding genetic information into quantum states and utilizing quantum operations for selection, crossover, and mutation. This approach theoretically utilizes quantum superposition to explore multiple solution possibilities simultaneously and quantum entanglement to correlate solutions, potentially leading to faster convergence and improved optimization performance. The paper outlines the theoretical framework, the algorithmic steps of the QGA, and discusses potential applications. The primary contribution is the conceptual framework and the proposed method, recognizing the nascent stage of QGA research and presenting a novel exploration of its potential.

title: ## Balearic Shrew Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BSMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Balearic Shrew Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BSMOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Balearic shrew ( *Crocidura balearica*). The algorithm utilizes a combination of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and a simulated annealing (SA) approach, incorporating elements of the shrew's navigation strategy – specifically, its reliance on scent marking and memory of previously visited locations – to enhance exploration and exploitation capabilities. BSMOA's core mechanism involves a 'scent map' representing the positions of particles, updated dynamically based on particle velocities and a local memory system. The algorithm aims to improve upon existing metaheuristic methods by addressing limitations in premature convergence and stagnation, particularly in complex, multi-dimensional optimization problems. The performance of BSMOA is demonstrated through simulations on a variety of benchmark functions, showcasing its effectiveness in achieving global optima and its robustness to different parameter settings. The algorithm's performance is evaluated against established metaheuristic techniques such as PSO, Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Differential Evolution (DE). Results demonstrate that BSMOA offers competitive performance with a simplified implementation, indicating its potential for further development and application in diverse optimization fields.

abstract: This paper explores the application of chaos field clustering to identify and analyze patterns within chaotic systems. This approach aims to provide a robust and efficient method for uncovering hidden structures and relationships within complex systems exhibiting chaotic dynamics. title: Arc Mountain Wood Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of a Rodent
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Arc Mountain Wood Mouse" (AMWM), inspired by the foraging behavior of the wood mouse ( *Apodemus sylvaticus* ) in mountainous regions. AMWM leverages the rodent's unique strategy of navigating complex terrains by iteratively selecting promising areas, exploring the search space, and adjusting its path based on local environmental conditions. The algorithm incorporates elements of both Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) with a novel "mountain climbing" mechanism to simulate the mouse's adaptation to varying slopes and obstacles. The core of AMWM lies in a dynamically adjusted 'mountain gradient' estimation, which guides the movement of the decision-making agents. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and provides a conceptual overview of its implementation. We demonstrate the algorithm's potential through theoretical analysis and discuss its strengths and limitations, positioning it as a promising approach for a variety of optimization problems.
